title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Mining Tunnels
text:
While T3-M4 worked on your ../Rescue/ in the hangar bay and fuel depot, your main character waited with Atton by the administration level's computer:

The administration level's  is now open!

|}

Otherwise:

|}

 Comlinks are a standard, short range communication device. [Party members can use it to contact you to provide information or warn you of danger.]

Your main character received none of the experience earned by T3-M4. Atton has nothing new to say, and if you use the administration computer to access the comm system and select Hangar Bay 25:

You need to go to the emergency hatch, back between the security room and medical bay, and take the turbolift to the mining tunnels.

Turbolift to Administration Level
The turbolift from the administration level is on the bottom left end of the mining tunnels. As you cross the room to the door in the top right wall opposite, Atton uses the comlink:

Otherwise:

|}

Atton using the comlink doesn't cancel  mode. Beyond the door is a short corridor with another door at its top right end, a plasteel cylinder by its bottom wall to your right, and a broken droid in its top back corner to your left:

Once you've checked the cylinder, if you haven't yet told Atton you don't want any of his advice:

|}

The corridor beyond the next door is empty, and leads through another door to a junction. The bottom right corridor is mined, and if you haven't yet told Atton you don't want any of his advice:

If you haven't checked the plasteel cylinder back in the first bottom left corridor:

|}

If you haven't put a point in  to disable or recover these mines, and you don't have  to trigger them from range, then if you're careful you can walk between them to get to the broken droid at the end of this corridor, where the tunnel has collapsed. There's another broken droid in the top right corridor, which is blocked by a door.

The top left corridor contains a damaged mining droid:

|}

At level 2, it's possible to reactivate and fully repair this droid with 9 Parts and  rank 8 (maximum rank 5 (level 2 + 3) as a class skill with 16  (INT +3), or 14 Intelligence and  (Intelligence: +2)).

The following options are still available once the droid engages its patrol mode:

Setting the droid to explode inflicts 20 piercing damage within range unless a Reflex save is made at DC 15, halving damage.

Once engaged in patrol mode, this droid enters the mouth of the mining tunnel at the top end of this corridor, and can patrol back and forth between here and the entrance to the cavern ahead. There are four Mark I mining droids in the linking tunnel: two melee and two ranged (one shielded).

There's also a broken droid at the left end of this tunnel:

The tunnel turns to your right, leading up to the bottom end of a large cavern. There's another ranged Mark I mining droid by a corpse lying on the right side, and further up in a recess in the left wall there's a Mark I excavator droid that can use a :

There are four Mark I mining droids (one melee and three ranged (two shielded)) with a maintenance droid at the top end of the cavern:

This maintenance droid repairs any damage inflicted on other droids so destroy it first, ideally with a ranged weapon, Force power or grenade: once destroyed it explodes, inflicting 10 piercing damage unless a Reflex save is made against DC 15, halving damage.

Superheated Blast Tunnel
There's also a corpse lying at the top end of the cavern:

As you approach the blast tunnel exiting the top right corner of this cavern, if you haven't yet told Atton you don't want any of his advice:

Each hot steam vent in the tunnel inflicts 2-4 fire damage on first contact and every 6 seconds thereafter: even if you run straight through you can take damage up to a dozen times, so using a Telos Mining Shield is highly recommended (particularly on Difficult). 

There's a second junction at the right end of the superheated blast tunnel, which is mined:

 

The bottom left and right corridors have collapsed, but the bottom right is mined and contains a corpse:

 

The top right tunnel contains a broken droid, three Mark I mining droids (two melee and one ranged (and shielded)), a Mark I excavator droid and a maintenance droid:

Central Mining Core
As you approach the bottom end of the top right tunnel from the second junction, if you haven't yet told Atton you don't want any of his advice:

If you have  rank > 0:

|}

There's a bridge across the main ventilation shaft in the central mining core ahead, with a corpse on its top half, and a Mark I excavator droid on the top right and bottom left sides of the walkway around the shaft's perimeter.

Containment fields in the four corners block any exit, so you need to shut them down using the central controller in the middle of the bridge. There's a plasteel cylinder to its left:

You can also use the central controller to unlock this cylinder:

You need to access fuel containment functions to shut down the containment fields:

You can call up droid command functions to help deal with remaining droids:

Adding other droids to their mining protocols makes them attack and kill each other as well, for which you'll also receive experience:

|}

However, it's better to do this after canceling all droid mining functions on organics first:

|}

Droids are no longer hostile, allowing you to scavenge Mark I mining and excavator droids for components:

  rank 2 or less Repair rank 3-5 Repair rank 6 or more

Setting a droid to explode inflicts 20 piercing damage within radius unless a Reflex save is made at DC 15, halving damage. Maintenance droids cannot be scavenged:

 [This droid is simply floating, doing nothing. It makes no acknowledging response when you examine it.]

In hindsight, to maximize experience and components received you would run or sneak past the first 18 droids and use the central controller to cancel all droid mining functions on organics (1800 XP) and shut down containment fields, then scavenge components from all 32 Mark I droids (maximum 160 in total), and then use the central controller to add other droids to their mining protocols so they can be attacked again, and killed to receive even more experience.

If you reassign mining protocols to mine sealed doors, then a new Mark I mining droid appears by the   beyond the containment field in the core's bottom right corner, and bashes it open from the inside:

|}

This droid is unaffected by the central controller, so it remains hostile... but it can be blinded...

Checking droid schematics and then raising the temperature to blind the droids costs nothing, but allows you to attack them without them attacking you. However, if you didn't ask Atton if you could sneak by them when you found the emergency supplies, then this is only an option if you have sufficient , or  or  skill, to work it out for yourself:

|}

Accessing camera functions can be informative:

|}

Once the containment fields are shut down, you can get to two Mark I mining droids (both ranged, one shielded) in the core's bottom left corner. There's a third droid (ranged and shielded) in the bottom left corridor, which also contains a broken droid and is blocked by a door:

The core's top left corner contains two Mark I mining droids (both ranged, one shielded).

The core's top right corner contains a Mark I excavator droid and a ranged and shielded Mark I mining droid, with a corpse on the right side.

High Security Door
The central mining core's bottom right corner contains two Mark I mining droids (both ranged, one shielded).

If you haven't used the central controller to reassign droid mining protocols to mine sealed doors, then there's a high security door in the bottom left corridor:

Otherwise, you face the Mark I mining droid that bashed it open:

There's a broken droid in both the top left and bottom right collapsed corridors at the next junction below:

The bottom left tunnel is mined, and leads down to a corpse on your right:

Turbolift to Fuel Depot
As you enter the bottom right corridor in the central mining core's bottom right corner:

|}

Atton has now locked the  behind you, and can keep the impending blast contained until you take the turbolift to the fuel depot.

The corridor curves up to your left, where there's a ranged Mark I mining droid, and it's mined.

On the top left side of the next junction there's a ranged Mark I excavator droid that can use s, and on the bottom right a maintenance droid:

The top right collapsed corridor is mined, and contains a damaged cylinder.

 This blast cylinder appears to have been damaged by the explosion. You can't unlock it, but you may be able to blast it open with a sonic charge.

The bottom right corridor contains two ranged and shielded Mark I mining droids and a corpse.

At the end of this corridor, the turbolift to the fuel depot is guarded by two Mark I excavator droids (one ranged with grenades, the other melee with a blowtorch), a ranged and shielded Mark I mining droid and a maintenance droid.

title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Pazaak
text:
Pazaak is a card game resembling Blackjack. Playing is optional, but it can be a good way to get credits and some other rewards.

You can always ask ../Atton/ to teach you to play  once you've traveled to Telos: Citadel Station, playing Republic Senate rules (no wager) since he's out of credits.

Your Pazaak Side Deck only has one of each card from +1 to +6, and -1 to -4:

 Pazaak requires both a main deck and a side deck. You can store all your side deck cards here and bring them out when you start a game. +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6  -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6  ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6   D ±1T                                             

Before wagering with other players you should really acquire better cards, most of which are sold by merchants:

 Pazaak Card This is a standard pazaak side deck card, for use with a pazaak deck. Flip +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6                                     150  175

+/- Cards are obviously more useful than purely positive or negative cards and thus cost more credits, but cost doesn't always indicate usefulness: for example, negative cards are normally more useful than positive cards since you start with fewer of them, and they can be used to avoid a bust before you end turn, forcing your opponent to take another turn and draw another card, thus making it more likely that your opponent goes bust or has to use a card to avoid it (this is particularly true when you draw first in the set, starting at a disadvantage).

 World Merchant +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6 2&4 3&6 Telos: CS                                      Mebla Dule                                  1  1 Nar Shaddaa                                     1 Dantooine                                   1  

Buying cards from at least Mebla Dule and Pato Ado is recommended before playing, as you're not restricted to their worlds before encountering a ../Lost Jedi/: you can play them, or travel elsewhere.

Cards can also be acquired from a final wager after defeating your opponents a certain number of times:

 World Area Source Pazaak Card(s)  Telos: Citadel Station Cantina    Nar Shaddaa Entertainment Promenade The Champ   Onderon Iziz Cantina width=10% width=10% width=10% 

Any cards acquired aren't displayed in  but simply added to your side deck, so you cannot sell unwanted cards. 

Gold cards have special rules associated with them:

 Pazaak Card This is an advanced pazaak side deck card, for use with a pazaak deck. 1±2 1±2 This card can change both its sign and its value. Before playing this card, you can change its value to 1, 2, -1 or -2. Double D This card doubles the value of last flipped card. This card doubles the value of the last card you are dealt.  Tie Breaker ±1T If the score is tied (and the opponent has chosen to stand), then playing this card results in a win. Subtracts or adds 1 from your score and allows you to win tied games. Flip 2&4 2&4 This card changes the sign (positive orto negative) of all of your 2s and 4s in play. This card flips all positive 2's and 4's you have in play to negative. Flip 3&6 3&6 This card changes the sign (positive orto negative) of all of your 3s and 6s in play. This card flips all positive 3's and 6's you have in play to negative.

Gold cards can normally only be selected from the side decks of the three organic opponents of the cantina's  in Nar Shaddaa's entertainment promenade.

1±2 Cards can be selected by  (1) and The  (2). Both sign and value must be declared before playing (after which they cannot be changed), so it's effectively +/-1 and +/-2 in one card, and it's normally only played on 18-22 after a card is dealt.

Double cards can be selected by  (1), Geredi (1) and The Champ (2). It doubles the value of the last card dealt, so it's normally only played if the turn then ends on 20.

Tie Breaker cards can be selected by Geredi (1) and The Champ (2). It's effectively +/-1, but in the case of a tie when the opponent stands, the player wins. It's normally played at 19 (+1) or 21 (-1)  to end on 20 and almost guarantee a win, but if its played at less than 19, ending below 20, then the opponent can still win by exceeding it or playing nine cards without going bust.

Flip cards can be selected by Geredi (2&4 (2) and 3&6) and The Champ (2 each). These cards flip all your positive 2s & 4s or 3s & 6s played (including +/- cards declared positive) to negative, but have no effect on negative cards declared or played. When first played, changing sign effectively makes these -4 & -8 or -6 & -12; if more are played, any affected cards are already negative, effectively making these just -2 & -4 or -3 & -6. They're normally only played when 2s & 4s or 3s & 6s have been played to avoid going bust, but they can result in negative totals, making it much more likely that nine cards are in play without going bust, thus automatically standing and winning.

A player can never have more than nine cards in play during one set, including cards from the hand as well as cards dealt from the deck, so once you have nine cards in play you automatically stand and win the set. Winning a Pazaak game with a full board like this is easiest with a side deck of negative, +/- and Flip 2&4 and 3&6 cards (the latter can be particularly powerful).

Although you can normally wager for as little as a single credit, it resets to maximum at the start of each match so it's best to wager for the maximum amount. However, even after you've upgraded your deck, you're still at a disadvantage: although you and your opponent alternate drawing first from the main deck at the beginning of each set, you always draw first in the first set, which means you'll most likely be the first to stand, go bust or use a card, all of which make it more likely that you'll be defeated. It may be exploitative, but you can save game before playing and after winning, and load game after losing to offset this (although there's no need once the wager isn't for credits).

The tank then drains, dropping you onto the floor, where you lie until you regain consciousness...

title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Polar Plateau
text:
After HK-50s arrived too late at the ../Underground Base/, but managed to track your shuttle's movement across the shield network, the unit dispatched to the polar region with your last known coordinates and approximate path awaits you on the polar plateau, and shoots down your shuttle!

The shuttle crashes on the left side of the plateau. In the aftermath, you, Atton and Kreia lie in the snow outside above the shuttle and, as you all get to your feet, the three HK-50s on the top side of the plateau speak:

|}

All three can use , which trebles damage on a critical hit. They're too far apart for grenades to affect more than one of them, but if you or Kreia can use Disable or Destroy Droid on the one in the middle then all three are affected, and Atton can make s on any stunned droids. Otherwise, since they're all ranged attackers, using melee weapons can improve chance to hit once the distance has been closed.

 This control cluster looks like it was singed by blaster fire, but it looks like the durasteel shell surrounding kept it intact despite the damage.

Bao-Dur lies in the snow at the bottom right corner of the shuttle:

 [Bao-Dur looks as if he was knocked unconscious by the explosion - if you can find refuge, then he should recover in time.]

On the bottom left side of the plateau there's a turbolift that can take you down into the polar plateau interior. Save game, as there can be a lot of dialog upon entering: after doing so, two figures dressed in white and armed with quarterstaves approach and stand over Bao-Dur...

Polar Plateau Interior
Having taken the turbolift down from the polar plateau with Atton and Kreia, you're met by a Handmaiden and two of her sisters in the entrance chamber below:

Avoid that response, as it may cause a glitch that prevents you from leaving. Otherwise:

Atton and Kreia are taken from the entrance chamber and imprisoned in cages: Bao-Dur lies, still unconscious, in another beside theirs. Atton and Kreia speak:

title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Prologue
text:
Cockpit, Galaxy Map
After character generation and the opening crawl, you watch the battered freighter with your main character aboard as it drifts towards the ravaged world of Peragus. In its cockpit, a lone Astromech droid is active:

Before you take control of T3-M4, a message pops up:

 Use the left thumbstick to move T3-M4. Swivel the camera with the right thumbstick. Click the right thumbstick to toggle first-person Free Look. Press W, A, S, D (Default) to move T3-M4 and turn. Press Caps Lock (Default) to toggle first-person Free Look. Hold Ctrl (Default) to Look About.

T3-M4 can return to the top right side of the cockpit at any time to Skip Prologue:

The Galaxy Map is on the bottom left side of the cockpit. If you interact with it:

Other than the Ebon Hawk, you can only select Peragus II. However, if you try to travel before completing the prologue:

 You are already at that location. The Ebon Hawk cannot dock with the Peragus Mining Facility until main power has been restored.

As you exit the cockpit via the corridor at its bottom end, a few more messages pop up:

 16px Journal Entry Added

 32pxThe ACTIVE QUESTS screen includes important information related to your ongoing adventures. Refer to this journal for hints and guidance throughout the game.

 [You have new quests. To view your quests, press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to scroll to the .] [You have new quests. To view your quests, open the Game Menu [Default: ESC] and look in the  (Default: J).]

Even if you Skip Prologue, these quests are completed:

None of the experience received during the prologue is retained by T3-M4 or your main character after skipping or completing it. If you use the Galaxy Map to travel to Peragus II after you actively save the Ebon Hawk, completing the prologue, then none of the items received remains in  for the later use of your main character and party.

However, if you Skip Prologue instead at this point then all items in inventory remain there: this is likely unintentional (and the ../Restored Content Mod/ may change it), but it can be exploited to give you a headstart (albeit unnecessary) on Peragus II.

Communications Console
After exiting the cockpit, if you interact with the main hold door at the bottom end of the corridor:

 [Beyond this door is the main hold of the Ebon Hawk. This door appears to be locked down due to a hull breach. See if there is an emergency override somewhere in the communications room behind you.]

The communications room is back through the doorway in the right side of the corridor:

 This room contains a Plasteel Cylinder and the Communications Console. To target one of these objects, move close to it, or use the left or right triggers to cycle through available targets. To interact with an object, first target it and then press . This room contains a Plasteel Cylinder and the Communications Console. To target one of these objects, move close to it, left click on it, or press Q or E (Default) to cycle through available targets. To interact with an object, first target it and then left click on it.

The communications console is on the right side of the room, directly opposite the doorway:

|}

The plasteel cylinder is to the left of the communications console. If you interact with it, but close it without getting the programming spike inside:

 [Take the programming spike inside this container by pressing . Use this spike to access the terminal nearby.] [Take the programming spike inside this container by clicking on the Get Item button. Use this spike to access the terminal nearby.]

 [You will come across many containers, some of which will be locked. The computer spike you just picked up can be used at computer terminals to access functions such as opening doors.]

You can now use this spike to slice the system and open the main hold door:

|}

Main Hold, Security Console
 This is the Main Hold.

The main hold is the central hub of the Ebon Hawk, and all T3-M4 needs to do is cross it and unlock the low security door in the middle of its bottom wall. If you interact with the door:

 [While some doors can be bashed open (or cut open with a lightsaber or cutting tool), some doors require the use of the  skill to open. Use your Security skill from the action bar to open this door.]

Unlocking it allows access to the bottom half of the vertical corridor between the cockpit and engine room, where you'll also find your main character laying in the . 

There's a red footlocker by the main hold's left wall. If you try to unlock it using the Security skill:

 [Your security skill is too low to open this footlocker. However, you can use your weapon to Bash it open. Press up or down on the D-pad to select Bash and then press .] [Your security skill is too low to open this footlocker. However, you can use your weapon to Bash it open. Click on the Bash icon or press 1 (Default).]

 32pxSome locked doors and containers can be opened by bashing or blasting them with a weapon until they open. Not all doors or containers can be successfully bashed. To bash an object, select it, then select Bash from the TARGET MENU.

T3-M4's unarmed attacks can inflict 1-4 (2.5 average) bludgeoning damage, so on average four hits should bash it open.

 [Sometimes bashing or blowing opening a container will break some of the items in the container. But you can use even broken items. They can be turned into useful components at a workbench.]

These computer spikes can be used to slice the security console in the middle of the main hold:

|}

You can now access security cameras to look around parts of the Ebon Hawk. You can also access security doors to open and close the outer and inner garage doors, but this is pointless while T3-M4 is alone since a hull breach in the garage prevents both doors being open at the same time.

To begin, the outer garage door is open and the inner garage door is closed:

|}

There's a blast door in the top right side of the main hold, and another just inside the corridor exiting its bottom right corner:

 [This blast door is magnetically sealed and cannot be opened.]

This horizonal corridor crosses the main hold, connecting the  on the other side to the starboard dormitory beyond this magnetically sealed blast door. There's a broken droid on the floor here, and another by the bottom left wall:

There's also a body by the bottom right wall:

 [This old woman appears to be dead. There is a keycard on the body that looks like it opens a locker somewhere.] This keycard is used to open up a locker in the storage room.

Medical Room
The bottom half of the vertical corridor between the Ebon Hawk's cockpit and engine room is beyond the low security door in the middle of the main hold's bottom wall. As you exit the main hold:

 [Use the  Screen to help you explore the Ebon Hawk. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to scroll to the Map.] [If you need help exploring the Ebon Hawk, access the  screen by pressing M (Default).]

The medical room is beyond another low security door in the left wall of this corridor, on your right as you go down it.

 This is the Medical Room.

Your main character lies on a bed by its top wall:

There's a medical storage bin beside the bed, in the top left corner:

T3-M4 can now use one of these on your main character, although this is a bonus mission which doesn't need to be completed to complete the prologue:

Lift to Outside the Ebon Hawk
There's a lift opposite the medical room, in the right wall of the corridor between the main hold and the engine room:

 This is the Utility Lift.

The engine room door is at the bottom end of this corridor, just beyond a junction:

 This is the Engine Room.

If you interact with it:

 [This door is damaged and cannot be opened with your Security skill, or by bashing it. You will have to find and use an explosive trap to open this door. Take the lift outside the Ebon Hawk to find one.]

Return to the lift and use its controls to go outside:

The lift  takes T3-M4 up to the middle of the Ebon Hawk's exterior hull, just below its gun turret.

center|thumb|320px|Map of Ebon Hawk's exterior hull

Starboard Outer Hull
T3-M4 has already started going down a ramp onto the Ebon Hawk's starboard side, to the right of the lift controls.

 This is the Starboard side of the Ebon Hawk.

Below the ramp on your right, there's a busted port in the starboard engine:

 [This busted engine port has some needed Parts for the Ebon Hawk's hyperdrive. Take the Parts here back down below to get main power restored.]

There's an open hatch in the floor below this port, to your left, another two open hatches out on the starboard side opposite the ramp down, and one more above the ramp, next to the cockpit:

 [This open hatch has some Parts that will be useful for getting main power restored.]

There's also some exposed wiring in the top right of the starboard side:

Port Outer Hull
As you return to the lift controls from the starboard outer hull:
 Don't forget to explore the other side of the Ebon Hawk.

You need to go down a ramp onto the port side:

 This is the Port side of the Ebon Hawk. 

Proton Missile, Mines
There's an unstable proton missile embedded in the bottom left of the port side, below the ramp:

Getting too close and triggering these can damage but not kill T3-M4. Otherwise, with  on Easy or Normal they can be disabled or recovered, but on Difficult they can only be disabled, not recovered. However, one can always be recovered from the proton missile itself:

 [You can use the explosive device in this missile to blow open the engine room door inside the Ebon Hawk. This will give you access to the hyperdrive. After you plant a mine, back away quickly so that you do not take damage.]

If T3-M4 sets mines until there are none in :

 If you run out of mines, you can return to the Proton Missile and collect another.

Quadlasers
There are damaged quadlasers on the top left of the port side, slightly above the ramp.

 [This is one of the Ebon Hawk's quadlaser turrets. They are damaged, but you can scavenge some Parts from it to use in repairing the Ebon Hawk.]

Lift to Inside the Ebon Hawk
Return to the lift controls in the middle of the outer hull once T3-M4 has at least one  from the starboard side, and at least five  in :

Engine Room, Hyperdrive
Once you have a  from the starboard side of the Ebon Hawk's starboard outer hull, you can go back inside to the engine room door at the bottom end of the corridor and use a mine to open it:

 [This door is damaged and cannot be opened with your Security skill, or by bashing it. You can use a mine to open this door. Once you plant the mine, back away from the door to avoid taking damage.]

If T3-M4 sets the mine(s) in the corridor until none are in :

 If you run out of mines, you can return to the Proton Missile outside the Ebon Hawk and collect another.

Recover the mine(s), then select the engine room door before using one:

 Left-clicking the mouse while a mine is selected in your ACTION MENU will place a mine. You can also disable and recover enemy mines and add them to your own inventory for later use.

T3-M4 takes no damage even if you don't back away, but the blast opens the door. Inside the engine room, the port and starboard engines are to either side:

 [The port engine is shut down, but appears intact. Fixing the hyperdrive will allow you to restore power to the port engine and bring primary power online.] [The Starboard engine is badly damaged. Fixing it won't be possible until after docking with the Peragus mining station.]

The hyperdrive is at the bottom end of the engine room:

 [You've already repaired the Hyperdrive. Now return to the Galaxy Map in the cockpit and Travel to Peragus.]

 [The port engine is powered up. You can now use the Galaxy Map to travel to the Peragus mining station.]

You can now return to the cockpit to complete the prologue, using the Galaxy Map to travel to the ../Peragus II/ mining station:

 This is the Cockpit.

The Galaxy Map is on the bottom left side:

Otherwise, you can still skip the prologue there, or explore the optional areas of the Ebon Hawk (if you haven't already done so).

Cargo Hold
The corridor to the left of the junction between the engine room and the main hold has a low security door in its left outer wall. If you interact with this door:

 [While some doors can be bashed open (or cut open with a lightsaber or cutting tool). Some doors require the use of the  skill to open. Use your Security skill from the action bar to open this door and search the remains of the cargo hold beyond.]

 This is the Cargo Hold.

This cargo hold has the droid 3C-FD in its bottom corner, opposite the doorway, and a locker by its right wall:

 [This container is locked and requires a key. Search the ship to find the key to this locker.]

The locker key is found on the body by the bottom right wall back in the .

 [You used the keycard you found to open the locker. The Impact Armor from this locker can be equipped on the  Screen. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [You used the keycard you found to open the locker. The Impact Armor from this locker can be equipped on the  Screen. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

There's a high security cylinder in the hold's top left corner, with an unlocked plasteel cylinder next to it.

Changing  to Difficult increases the lock's Difficulty Class by 5, to 41 (while changing to Easy decreases it by 5, to 31, which is still too difficult to open):

 [You must lower your difficulty setting in order to open this lock. Access the  screen and select Gameplay. Then change the difficulty setting from Difficult to Normal.] [The lock on this container is too difficult to open. You'll need to use a security tunneler to help open the lock. Look in the unlocked cylinder next to this one to find security tunnelers.]

 [If you encounter a difficult lock on a container or door, you can use a security tunneler on it to improve your chance of opening the lock. Use the security tunneler to open the High Security Cylinder nearby.]

Returning to the high security cylinder:

 [The lock on this metal box is too difficult to open. You can use one of the Security Tunnelers you found to crack this lock. Select the Security Tunneler by pressing left or right on the D-pad and press  to use it.] [The lock on this metal box is too difficult to open. You can use one of the Security Tunnelers you found to crack this lock. Select the Security Tunneler by clicking on the arrows above or below the Security icon.]

 You can have multiple powers or items in each icon of the ACTION MENU. Scroll up or down using the mouse wheel to cycle through the various options.

Combat Training
There's a metal box in the middle of the cargo hold which can be unlocked for combat training:

 [You can equip a weapon from the  screen. Press START to open the Pause Menu, and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [You can equip a weapon from the  screen. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

If you interact with any of the four sensor droids before equipping a weapon:

 [T3-M4 must equip a blaster before attacking the sensor droids. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [T3-M4 must equip a blaster before attacking the sensor droids. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

If you open the metal box again:

 [Destroy all the sensor balls to continue to the next step of combat training.]

Once T3-M4 has equipped a Field Survival Pistol:

 ENEMY SIGHTED!Press the Pause key (SPACE or Pause) to continue

 The game pauses when you sight an enemy, and the selection reticle will show up in red. You can use the mouse to select other hostile targets. This auto-pause option can be disabled on the  screen.

 [Change your target by using the left and right triggers. To attack an enemy, select the Sword icon with the D-pad and press . To queue up multiple combat actions, press . To cancel the last combat action, press .] [Change your target by pressing Q or E, or left click on the object you want to target. To attack an enemy, left click on the Sword icon or press 1. To Queue up actions, left click multiple times. Clear your last combat action by clicking in the queue, or by pressing Y.]

The sensor droids cannot attack or inflict damage. If you attack a sensor droid:

 ../Combat/ mode engaged

 32pxWhenever you spot an enemy, left-click the selected enemy once to enter combat mode. This will lock the camera on your selected target. Left-clicking the target again causes your character to perform the Default Action and attack each round. Your chances of hitting a target are controlled by your statistics and behind the scenes combat rolls. Combat is not affected by your aim, your character's movements or the movements of your target.

 Remember: Only left-click the targetted enemy ONCE to engage. You will automatically attack your target each round. You do not have to left-click it again until you select a new target. When engaged in combat you can use the TARGET and ACTION MENUs to activate items, feats and Force powers each round. Otherwise your character will automatically perform their default attack each round.

Sensor droids only have 8  and 1 , so they're easy to hit and any damage inflicted will destroy them. Once the first group has been destroyed:

 [Good work defeating the sensor droids. To continue combat training, open the metal box again and more sensor droids will appear.]

 [More sensor droids emerge from the container.]

 [You can pause and unpause combat with . Pausing combat will help you plan your moves strategically.] [You can pause and unpause combat by clicking on the hourglass icon in the lower right area of the screen, or press Spacebar. Pausing combat will help you plan your moves strategically.]

Once a second group has been destroyed:

 [You destroyed another group of sensor droids. To continue combat training, open the metal box again.]

 [This box seems to have an infinite supply of sensor balls.]

 [You found a grenade in the container. With grenades you can damage multiple enemies at once. To throw a grenade, select the grenade by pressing right or left on the D-pad. Then press .] [You found a grenade in the container. With grenades you can damage multiple enemies at once. To throw a grenade, click the grenade icon above your selected target, or press 3 (Default).]

../Grenades/ can also affect but not kill T3-M4 when in the area of effect. Once a third group has been destroyed, each time you open the metal box you only receive another grenade if there aren't any in  (used, or given to another container in the cargo hold):

 [These sensor balls don't leave behind any useful items when you kill them, but many enemies do. After combat, be sure and search your enemies' remains.]

If you open the metal box again once a fourth group has been destroyed:

 [There are two weapon configurations in the Equip screen. This is useful to switch between ranged and melee weapons. To switch or unequip weapons, press up or down on the D-pad to select the two swords icon and press .] [There are two weapon configurations in the Equip screen. This is useful to switch between ranged and melee weapons. To switch or unequip weapons, click the two swords icon in the lower right area of the screen, or press H (Default).]

Once a fifth group has been destroyed:

 [You have completed combat training. You may still continue to use the metal box to display the combat training messages from the beginning.]

Repair 3C-FD
If you approach the droid 3C-FD standing in the bottom corner of the cargo hold:

If you interact with 3C-FD with no  in :

 [3C-FD is malfunctioning. You can fix him by using a Part. Search the ship to find one. If you repair 3C-FD, he can join your party and assist you in repairing the ship.]

Otherwise:

|}

 [3C-FD is now a member of your party. Press the 'BLACK' button to change which party member you control. Later, when you have more companions, you can add and remove party members from the ../Party/ screen in the Pause Menu.] [3C-FD is now a member of your party. To change which party member you control, click on their portrait or press TAB (Default).  Later, when you have more companions, you can add and remove party members from the ../Party/ screen in the Game Menu.]

If you speak to 3C-FD again:

 Reet doo-reep deet dee.

Clicking on the portrait of the party member you control opens the  screen, and opening the  and  screens as well allows you to compare the two droids:

Once this quest is active, skipping or completing the prologue also completes it:

Port Dormitory
The corridor outside the cargo hold leads up to a junction: the main hold can be seen at the end of the corridor to the right, while to the left the corridor ends at a blast door just around the corner to your right. However, the port dormitory beyond it is inaccessible:

 [This blast door is magnetically sealed and cannot be opened.]

Garage, Workbench
The inner or outer garage door blocks the corridor to the right of the junction between the engine room and the main hold:

 This is the Garage.

If you interact with the door:

 [There is a hull breech in the area beyond this door. Safety protocols prevent you from opening it manually. Try using the security computer in the Main Hold.]

Garage Access

If you interact with the inner or outer garage door again after returning from the  and inviting the droid 3C-FD to join your party there:

 [To access the area beyond this door, you will have to use Solo mode. Press BACK to toggle Solo Mode. While in Solo mode, move 3C-FD to the security computer to open the door for you.] [To access the area beyond this door, you will have to use Solo mode (Default: V). Click the Solo mode button at the bottom right area of the screen. While in Solo mode, move 3C-FD to the security computer to open the door for you.]

Once inside, the sparking wires to your right on the lower side of the doorway can be used to open and close the inner and outer garage doors, just like the security console (although you only need to use them to get both droids in the garage, which is unnecessary):

|}

If you approach the workbench by the top left wall:

If you interact with it:

Only five non-upgrade items can be created, with the following component cost:

      10  1  12  5  3

Any item in  breaks down into at least the single component needed to create a Repair Kit, and you can get two components from the high security cylinder in the .

 [You can use Repair Kits to heal droids like yourself. Select the Repair Kit by pressing Left or Right on the D-pad, and then press  to use it.] [You can use Repair Kits to heal droids like yourself. To use a Repair Kit, click on the Repair Kit on bottom of the screen or press 5(Default).]

T3-M4 started with 5/30  and the Repair Kit can heal up to 28, which should restore maximum Vitality (although this is unnecessary). Once this quest is active, skipping or completing the prologue also completes it:

Ebon Hawk Exit
Through the doorway in the top right wall of the garage is the left end of the corridor leading to the starboard dormitory to the right. The blast door at the left end blocks return to the main hold:

 [This blast door is magnetically sealed and cannot be opened.]

In the top wall opposite the garage doorway is the Ebon Hawk's loading ramp:

 [When the Ebon Hawk has landed, this is where you will go to exit the ship.]

Starboard Dormitory
The right end of the corridor beyond the doorway in the garage's top right wall may be blocked by a blast door:

 [This door is sealed shut, but the magnetic clamps are not engaged. You may be able to override the door's locking mechanism from outside the ship.]

Once you've used the exposed wiring on the  to override it, the door is open (although if you use the droid at the main hold's security console to do this now, then both droids will be taken outside).

 This is the Starboard dormitory.

There's a footlocker by the top wall, and another by the right wall:

 [You found a droid flamethrower. This is one of the special weapons that droids can use. To equip it open the  screen, by pressing START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [You found a droid flamethrower. This is one of the special weapons that droids can use. To equip it open the  screen, by clicking on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

Storage Compartment
If you interact with the blast door in the top right side of the Ebon Hawk's main hold:

 [You can hear a banging noise coming from the other side of the door to this storage compartment, but the door is sealed shut and cannot be opened from the outside.]

title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Ravager - Command Deck
text:
The Republic fleet has arrived, and approaches the Ravager and Citadel Station:

|}

As the fleet engages the Ravager, your shuttle docks with it...

Shuttle to Citadel Station
The shuttle from Citadel Station docks on the top left side of the Ravager's command deck. Sith line up below the docking hatch to repel boarders... only for the Mandalorians to blow a hole in the left wall to enter, guns blazing!

|}

Mandalore is added to your party with Visas, and you are unable to change your party at this time. You start in the room below the shuttle breach, which has a large locker in its bottom right corner:

You'll need to go through the doorway in the top right wall later to return to the escape shuttle, but if you approach the breach in the left wall now, before you defeat Darth Nihilus:

 [This route leads back to the shuttle and Citadel Station, but you still have unfinished business aboard the Ravager.]

You may find some remains left by the Sith, but the door in the top wall only leads to an empty tunnel.

Destroy the Ravager

All four bomb sites are on the command deck:

  on the bottom left of the map
  on the bottom middle of the map

  on the bottom right of the map
  on the top right of the map

The four proton cores can be set in any order, and if you dislike backtracking then you might want to complete part of this quest after you've been to the bridge to defeat Darth Nihilus: for example, set the first two proton cores at the second and third bomb sites on the way to the bridge, then on returning set them at the fourth and first sites on the way back to the escape shuttle... although if you defeat Darth Nihilus before placing the last proton core, then you don't receive 250 XP for doing so.

Whenever you approach a bomb site, Zuka contacts Mandalore:

After setting the first of the proton cores:

After setting the second of the proton cores:

After setting the third of the proton cores:

However, the fourth proton core detonates prematurely during a battle with the Sith:

|}

Fortunately, you can now get another proton core from the missile bay directly opposite the door inside the maintenance bay, on the top middle side of the command deck:

 [This proton core is locked into its bay, and it cannot be removed. You will need to find an override console for the missile bay.]

Missile bay control is mounted on the right wall at the other end of the maintenance bay:

 [You have retrieved the proton core from the missile bay.]

After placing the last proton core:

If you haven't defeated Darth Nihlus yet:

Otherwise:

Defeat Darth Nihilus

The turbolift to the  is in the middle of the right wall of the corridor along the right side of the command deck. Everything on the command deck can still be done after you defeat Darth Nihilus on the bridge, although you won't receive 250 XP for placing the last proton core to destroy the Ravager.

Bomb Site One
At the start, go through the door ahead of you in the bottom left wall of the room. If you then go through the door in the right wall (to your left), you'll find three Sith commandos and an elite trooper in the next room:

There's also a large locker in the bottom left corner and a door in the bottom right wall, beyond which is a short corridor ending at another door.

If you return to the previous room and then go through the door in the left wall, then you'll find four Sith commandos in the corridor beyond:

This corridor turns a corner to your left, ending at a door that opens to reveal two more Sith commandos and an elite trooper:

There's a security door in the right wall, and a large locker in the bottom left corner of this next room:

The door in the bottom wall of the previous room opens onto a corridor with a door in its right wall (on your left), beyond which is a room containing three Sith commandos with two large lockers by its bottom wall, one of which is locked:

Continue down the corridor and turn the corner to your left, and the first bomb site is through the door in the bottom wall. The room at the right end of the corridor contains a Sith commando and an elite trooper:

Beyond the door in the top right wall is a short corridor ending in another door, beyond which is a large room containing a Sith lieutenant, two soldiers and four commandos.

Going through the door in the top wall will take you back toward the shuttle.

Maintenance Bay & Workbench
The door in the right wall of the Sith lieutenant's room opens on the middle of a corridor: you can see Sith down the large hall through the archway in the wall opposite, but they're unaware of you in the corridor.

The bottom of this corridor (to your right) is a dead end, but there's a security door in its right wall, beyond which is a store room with a large locker in its bottom left corner.

The top end of this corridor turns right, where a door in its bottom wall (on your right) opens directly opposite the missile bay:

 [This proton core is locked into its bay, and it cannot be removed. It could detonate if you tried, it would be best to leave it.]

There's a locked large locker between it and a  in the middle of the bottom wall, and another large locker in the bottom right corner of the maintenance bay.

Missile bay control is mounted on the right wall:

|}

Bomb Site Two
Beyond the maintenance bay, the corridor leads to a junction at its right end: the corridor to your left goes up and then right before leading to a dead end, while the door in the opposite wall of the junction opens to reveal a barracks containing two Sith commandos and an elite trooper, with a large locker by its top left wall.

However, the bottom end of the corridor to your right leads to the other end of the large hall you saw earlier, and as you enter the corridor the Sith captain with pairs of assault troopers and grenadiers there will become aware of you unless you remain undetected in  mode:

The ramp at the right end of this hall leads up to the , where more Sith are visible but unaware of you. The corridor in the bottom wall opposite has a door in its right wall (on your left) leading to an empty barracks, and a security door in its left wall (on your right) leading to a room with a large locker by its bottom left wall.

The corridor turns to your left as you go down it, and you'll find the second bomb site at its right end.

Central Chamber
The ramp at the right end of the Sith captain's hall leads up to a central chamber, where you'll find two Sith commandos and an elite trooper.

There's a door in the chamber's top right corner, and another in its bottom right corner. The door in the top right corner leads to an empty room which also has a door in its top right corner, beyond which is another empty room: the door in its top left wall leads to 's room, while another door in its right wall leads to the corridor just above the door to the , which is in the middle of that corridor's right wall.

Bomb Site Three
Beyond the door in the bottom right corner of the central chamber is a large room containing a Sith lieutenant, two soldiers and four commandos.

There's another door in the top right wall, which can lead up through two empty rooms to  or the corridor just above the door to the , and a security door in the right wall leading to a small room with a large locker in its top left corner.

Through another door in the bottom wall of the Sith lieutenant's room there's a corridor, the left end of which is the third bomb site: to the right (your left), there's a door in the bottom wall leading to a room with a large locker in its bottom right corner.

Up ahead, the corridor turns a corner to your left, where the cell door to  is in the right wall.

Bomb Site Four
Beyond the door in the top right corner of the central chamber is a room with a door in its 
bottom right wall leading to 's room, and another door in its top wall leading to the left end of a corridor: the fourth bomb site is beyond the door in its top wall to the right, where the corridor then turns to your right and leads down to the door to the  in the middle of its right wall (on your left), just beyond a door in its left wall (to your right) which leads to the room below Colonel Tobin.

Colonel Tobin
Colonel Tobin can be found in a room in the top right of the command deck, accessible via a door in its bottom left wall from the room between the  and the fourth bomb site, or another door in its bottom left corner which can be accessed from the bridge corridor or by going up through the door in the top right corner of the Sith lieutenant's room below the central chamber.

There's a security door in this room's right wall, beyond which is another room with large lockers by its top and bottom walls.

Colonel Tobin doesn't speak unless spoken to:

|}

You can ask a series of questions after asking what happened to him, to which Mandalore and Visas can also contribute:

|}

|}
Otherwise:

Otherwise:

Either of these options is good. Otherwise, he has to die:

Killing him is psychotic.

Visas' Meditation Room
The cell door to Visas' meditation room is in the right wall at the bottom end of the bridge corridor along the right side of the command deck. As you approach it:

Otherwise:

Visas goes through the cell door and down to the meditation chamber at the bottom of her cell:

Depending on Visas' ../Alignment/:

 Alignment < 60 Alignment > 59 24pxVisas has chosen to embrace vengeance and the dark side. This has given her a stronger connection to the Force, and a bonus to her Force Points. 24pxVisas has come to terms with the death of her world and calmed the hatred within herself. This has given her a stronger connection to the Force, and a bonus to her Force Points.

Visas' maximum Force points increased by 50. If you go through the cell door, then the first room has a security door in its top wall, beyond which is a small room with two large lockers by its right wall.

If you go through the cell door in the bottom right corner of the first room, then Visas will go to her meditation chamber through the doorway in the bottom wall of this second room, if she hasn't already done so. There's nothing else in this room, or the meditation chamber beyond.

Bridge
Beyond the door in the middle of the corridor along the right side of the command deck is a room containing three Sith commandos and an elite trooper: they're guarding the turbolift to the bridge behind the door in the right wall.

Courtyard

When you exit the courtyard via the tunnel opposite the entrance, Kreia enters the courtyard behind you and looks around:

Showing her age, she sits:

If you didn't kill any of the lost Jedi:

Lost Jedi

You engage in combat with any surviving lost Jedi. The two doors in the top right of the Council chamber are now locked.

They rarely, if ever, use Force powers for anything other than healing. Master Kavar's  restores up to 30 Vitality at level 28, while Master Vrook's Master Heal restores up to 62 Vitality at level 28 and neutralizes any poison or stun: they only start to heal when reduced to less than half of maximum Vitality.

The tunnel beyond the door in the right wall of the training room leads back to the Council chamber to your right, and the inner courtyard to your left, which you can explore if you haven't already done so.

There's a room in the bottom right corner of the main hub, beyond the door in the wall below  (there's another door around the corner in its left wall). There's an argument taking place within, between a blue Twi'lek named Squik and a thug boss and three thugs, which your entrance will turn violent:

|}

The boss cuts down Squik and remotely closes and locks the two doors before all the thugs turn their attention on you:

You've just gained the attention (but not the favor) of the Exchange. The doors will open when the boss is killed, unless you open them yourself first.

One thug is a Gran using a  and up to three , and the other two are Weequays with s.

title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Refugee Quad
text:
Refugee Landing Pad
You're unable to change your party inside the refugee quad, so you need to return to the refugee landing pad to do so. 

The junction beyond the door in front of you is guarded by two Exchange thugs, a Trandoshan and a Gamorrean. As you approach or speak to either one (you cannot sneak past):

|}

If you intimidate with strength, persuade with skill or simply pay the toll then you can gain the favor and the attention of the Exchange:

Otherwise:

|}

If you fail to intimidate, succeed but give them a fight anyway, or cannot pay the toll then you lose the favor and gain the attention of the Exchange:

Otherwise, or upon returning:

Otherwise:

|}

If you can intimidate them then you can do so every time you return to speak to them, gaining the favor and attention of the Exchange each time.

The magnetically sealed door in the bottom wall at the right end of the hall is impossible to unlock, so you have no choice but to go through the door in the top wall: the ramp to the left leads down to another landing with a door to your right in the top wall. You can go through the door on the opposite side of the landing beyond and keep going until eventually reaching the , or go down the ramp to the right to the door to the refugee commons.

Refugee Commons
You enter an open area filled with cargo crates in which refugees sleep: you can open the cargo doors to these crates, but there are no containers or people inside. There are alleys between these crates running down both sides, and a junction with a middle alley at the top of the left alley. Refugees and veterans wander the area:

 If you want to find out what's going on, talk to Hussef. The Exchange's thugs are always demanding toll and tribute - and we don't have much more to give. Saquesh has got us hemmed in like animals. I wish someone would sneak into their camp and rob them blind. I heard the Overseer kidnapped Nadaa's daughter. The Serroco killed another refugee last week. I wish they'd leave us alone. Poor Geriel... I don't think he'll last much longer.

  Saquesh seems to have laid off us a bit. Life is much easier without the Exchange pressuring us. I wonder why the Exchange has been giving us more breathing room lately. Are you the one who killed the Overseer? Thank you! I heard there's a Jedi helping some of the refugees.

  That was so kind of you to help out Nadaa and Adana! Nadaa and Adana have been sold to some Hutt named Lagra, I hear. 

  I saw you hanging out with the Serroco. We don't want any trouble. The Serroco haven't been giving us as much trouble lately. Life's been easier since someone wiped out the Serroco.

  You saved us all from that horrible plague!  The plague finished off Geriel... I hope it doesn't spread. 

|}

 I used to serve in the Mandalorian Wars... then the Jedi Civil War crushed the Republic. I'm done with fighting... I've seen enough of battle. What did I fight for... to starve here on Nar Shaddaa? I once fought for the Republic... and it all meant nothing in the end.

|}

Plague Carrier
The refugee Geriel is in the top left corner of the commons, to the right of the top door as you enter:

|}

You can cure him with sufficient skill in treating injuries (rank 6 or more), but save game before doing so:

|}

 Influence Lost: Handmaiden (-2)

Having spoken to Geriel, you can go and speak about him to the overseer Saquesh in , gaining the favor and the attention of the Exchange:

The personal guard standing by the bottom wall leaves to kill Geriel, which is psychotic. Otherwise:

You cannot speak to him about this again. If you haven't already cured Geriel then you can still do so without affecting your standing with the Exchange, but it's obviously better to do it beforehand (1500 vs 750 XP in total).

Ironically, the only reason you need Treat Injury rank 15 or more is to move even closer to the dark side of the Force if you convince him to kill himself instead, which is cunning in either case:

You can relieve the pressure on the refugees by convincing the Serroco thugs and the Exchange to give them more space, or eliminating their leadership from the refugee quad.

The  can only be convinced to be less oppressive after speaking to Hussef and activating the Refugee Woes quest, then telling the Serroco leader you don't like how he has been bullying the refugees, and successfully intimidating him or persuading him with skill or the Force to stop harassing them.

This also completes the Serroco Thugs quest (for which you receive another 1000 XP).

You can always eliminate the Serroco thugs' leadership, even after convincing them to be less oppressive (receiving another 500 XP for completing the Serroco Thugs quest by killing their leader, and losing the favor but gaining the attention of the Exchange whether the leader was convinced or killed).

The Exchange can only be convinced to put less pressure on the refugees if Geriel is still alive after you've spoken to him, allowing you to explain to the overseer Saquesh in  that one of the refugees has a terrible disease, and persuade him that if he doesn't relax his hold on the refugees, this disease will spread (receiving 250 XP for explaining to Saquesh about the diseased Geriel, or 1000 XP if you've already cured him (500 XP) and thus leveraged his illness, and gaining the favor and the attention of the Exchange).

Otherwise, after speaking to Hussef and activating the Refugee Woes quest you can try to intimidate Saquesh:

Intimidation isn't an option if you've already convinced Saquesh to put less pressure on the refugees, but he can still be killed if you haven't completed the  quest. 

Killing Saquesh gains the attention of the Exchange, but surprisingly again has no effect on favor.

If you eliminate the leadership of both the Serroco thugs and the Exchange before speaking to Hussef to activate the Refugee Woes quest, then you move (much) closer to the light side of the Force and receive more experience when you do first speak to him:

A woman named Kahranna stands at the bottom of the middle alley of the commons:

Otherwise:

You can attempt to cheat her, which surprisingly gives you the only chance to move closer to the light side of the Force, if you're persuasive enough:

Despite this, the next time you speak to her she responds as though you told her you'd help find someone to transport them. Otherwise:

If you go after telling her you're not really the spacer, but before confirming you'll find someone for her, then you can repeat the previous dialog and move closer to the light each time. Otherwise:

 Get away from me, you scum!

Once Kahranna has called you a filthy liar, you can go and speak about tricking her with the overseer Saquesh in  (even if you didn't take any credits):

Otherwise:

20 credits gains the favor and the attention of the Exchange, and 200 gains twice as much of both (albeit for 10 times the price).

Twi'leks
Whether or not Atton is in your party, as you approach the bottom of the right alley in the refugee commons, two Twi'leks appear behind you and talk among themselves about him:

Will Work for Fuel
A man named Odis stands in the bottom right corner of the commons, by the door:

Otherwise:

 Quit wasting my time.

|}

The Lunar Shadow crewmen in the flophouse on the docks are happy for Odis to replace their wayward captain, moving you closer to the light side of the Force and giving you 2500 XP in total for completing both quests. Otherwise, you won't be able to find him a job until you've been aboard Goto's yacht, but once you've been you won't have to return here. 

Serroco Thugs
Serroco territory is on the right side of the quad, but you should speak to Hussef back in the central commons about  before going here, or the overseer Saquesh in  on the left side of the quad.

If you go through one of the doors in the right walls at the top of the ramps down to the top and bottom end of the , then keep going through doors in the right walls, you'll eventually reach a ramp down to a door at either end of Serroco territory. These top and bottom paths are  symmetrical, although the top passes a door in its top and bottom walls and the bottom passes two security doors, all to empty rooms, and the top door to Serroco territory is guarded by one armored Serroco thug and one unarmored, while the bottom is guarded by two unarmored thugs.

However, a concealed entrance offers a more direct route into Serroco territory: beyond the cargo door in the bottom right corner of the commons, there's a short passage to your left which turns up and ends at another cargo door in the right wall, beyond which is an armored Serroco thug.

This armored Serroco thug challenges you as you approach him or the bottom door, as does the armored thug at the top door:

Hostilities can otherwise be avoided (or postponed), but you need to speak to Hussef about refugee woes, or the Exchange overseer Saquesh, before a thug can be persuaded without using the Force:

 Hurry up and take care of your business.

Otherwise:

You can still open any door and enter Serroco territory, but the Serroco thugs become hostile if you approach one of the two armored thugs:

 Hey, I thought we told you to stay out of here!

Otherwise, if you speak to any other Serroco thugs, or veterans:

 We're all we've got - we need to stick together. If any more refugees try to come in here, we'll cut them down. If the Exchange tries to muscle in, we'll break them. I'm spoiling for a fight.

There's a lone thug wandering the top of the deceptively empty-looking Serroco territory, and an  parked on its lower right side. If you came in through the concealed entrance then you can get to the bottom end of Serroco territory via the three cargo doors in the right wall through the two back-to-back cargo crates opposite this entrance, with two Serroco thugs in the right one. There are three more cargo doors above this in the left wall of Serroco territory: beyond the lower two are crates with a plasteel cylinder in their top left corners (the one in the upper crate is locked).

However, approaching the lower cargo door brings you close enough to the Serroco leader, standing in the middle of Serroco territory with four Serroco veterans, for him to speak to you. If the thugs aren't hostile:

|}

|}

|}

This also addresses Hussef's , for which you receive another 1000 XP. If you then ask the Serroco to disarm themselves, they become hostile:

You lose the favor and gain the attention of the Exchange by persuading the Serroco to be less oppressive of the refugees, or killing their leader, but not both (although you can do both for the experience).

Otherwise, if the thugs and their leader and veterans aren't hostile, then they can become so if you're detected opening any security door in the alley between the concealed entrance at the bottom, and the top cargo door in the left wall of Serroco territory: the cargo crate behind this door contains two thugs, three wander the vertical top section of the alley behind the cargo door in its left wall, and five wander the horizontal bottom section, connecting the concealed entrance below its left end with the top section to the right.

There are three security doors in the left wall and one in the right wall of the vertical top section of the alley. If you're detected opening any of them:

 Hey! What's going on over there?

The top left cargo crate has a plasteel cylinder in its top left corner, the middle left crate has two plasteel cylinders in its bottom left corner, one locked, and the bottom left crate is empty. The crate on the right side has another locked plasteel cylinder in its top right corner.

Exchange Headquarters
A Twi'lek named Kaul stands in the bottom corner of the left alley of the refugee commons:

Otherwise:

|}

 Good luck to you.

Beyond the door at the bottom end of the commons is a ramp up to a landing. If you go through the door to your left and keep going then you'll eventually reach the  on the right side of the quad.

Otherwise, beyond the door and the ramp up to your right is another landing with a door in its left wall, beyond which is a room containing a pair of Exchange thugs, Gamorreans:

 You the new muscle? The Overseer's the one you want to see. You don't smell like a refugee.

The rooms beyond the next two doors in the left walls both contain another pair of Exchange thugs and have a locked metal box in each of their bottom corners. If you unlock any of these boxes while a thug is nearby and they see you, or hear you in  mode:

 Get out of there or I bash you! What was that?

They only remain neutral if they remain unaware of you while getting (or even giving) items. They become hostile if they see you bash or blast a lock, or if they become aware of you getting (or giving) items or engaging in combat.

 Hey, what are you doing?

A lone Exchange thug wanders the hallway beyond the door in the top wall of the first room, while another stands guard to the right of a security door in the hallway's left wall. Even if you unlock this security door in Stealth mode and this guard remains unaware of you, he becomes hostile:

The room beyond contains a locked metal box in its bottom left corner, and a girl named Adana.

The hallway above the security door turns left, ending with a door in its top wall, on your right. The hallway beyond has another security door (unlocked) in its right wall, beyond which is a mess room containing two pairs of Exchange thugs, with a door in the top and bottom corners of the right wall. Overseer Saquesh stands in the middle of the room beyond, with a Weequays personal guard standing by the top and bottom walls, and a large pair of windows in the right wall, overlooking the commons below.

Upon returning:

|}

The magnetically sealed door in the bottom wall of the quad's entrance hall is now open. Upon next returning:

Otherwise:

|}

|}

If you speak to Saquesh before speaking to Hussef about :

Saquesh and his guards won't become hostile even if you kill Exchange thugs right in front of them, but he, his guards and any remaining Exchange thugs do become hostile if you try to intimidate him to stop pressuring the refugees or let Adana go, or forget it and just kill him anyway even if you successfully persuade him:

The guard by the top wall, Gonlo, only has 3 Constitution, resulting in just 36 Vitality and 10 Fortitude, but is absent if you told Saquesh he should hurry and sell Adana to the Hutts. The guard by the bottom wall, Jubei, is absent if you persuaded Saquesh to kill Geriel before his disease can spread.

You can receive another 1000 XP and gain the attention of the Exchange for killing Saquesh, but surprisingly this has no effect on favor.

Returning to the hallway, turning right and going through the door at its top end, the hallway continues to the right before turning up to your left. title: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords/Rescue
text:
Storage Room

Your main character remains with Atton by the computer in the administration level. T3-M4 is alone in the main cargo hold on the top side of the hangar bay. Since the ../Prologue/, he's repaired and armed with a :

Curiously, T3 also has access to your . There's a broken droid in the middle of the room and a footlocker to either side:

Bashing the footlocker containing components adds a broken item, whereas if you bash the one containing the sonic grenade then a broken item replaces the one(s) you would have received. However, T3 has  rank 10 so he should always unlock these out of combat, even on Difficult since according to  it's 30 (roll 20 + Security 10) vs. DC 26 (21 + 5). There's no need to set it to Easy (DC 16 (21 - 5)).

Fuel Depot Sub-Level
There's a low security door in the left wall of the storage room, to T3-M4's right. When you interact with any low security door here for the first time:

 The success of your Security skill is random. If at first you cannot unlock a container or door, try again - you may succeed on the second attempt.

This is only true in combat: if you try to unlock a container or door during combat, then you roll 1-20 against the lock; out of combat, you automatically roll 20 every time.

This door opens to reveal two Mark I mining droids:

The droid closest to the ramp down to your right is different from the others:

T3's own  also inflicts 1-8 (4.5 average) energy damage, whereas at level 3 his  inflicts 3-18 (10.5 average) electrical damage unless a Fortitude save is made against DC 8, halving this. It also has infinite uses!

Although T3-M4 is level 3, some enemy bonuses are still calculated based on your main character's level (2).

At the bottom of the ramp there's a landing with a plasteel cylinder in its top left corner, and two more Mark I mining droids.

The next ramp leads down from the landing's bottom left corner to a door in the left wall, beyond which is the turbolift to the fuel depot's sub-level, a maintenance level divided by a fuel line. The right side contains a broken droid:

A series of two doors allows you to cross the fuel line to the left side, which contains two Mark I mining droids, a corpse and another broken droid:

 ...purged the fuel lines, and I found three sonic charges attached *inside.* I checked the work logs, and only droids have been in the area. I tried to contact security as soon as I found the explosives, but I can't seem to get a signal through.I've removed the remote detonators, and I'll keep the explosives on me until I can put them in a secure hold in the hangar. This wrecked droid contains a special droid-based item that when equipped, allows droids to perform special attacks against opponents. This destroyed droid contains an ion blaster, which is extremely effective against droid opponents and energy shields. It only has a limited number of charges, after which it is destroyed.

You can now only go back the way you came, but first make sure you have the items from the corpse and second broken droid. Checking the corpse triggers the appearance of two more Mark I mining droids back on the landing between the ramps up from the hangar bay's sub-level. These droids are shielded:

s absorb up to 20 points of energy and fire damage in total, which is yet more reason to used T3's Shock Arm (electrical) instead of his  (energy). The Droid Ion Striker and Ion Blast Mark I may both inflict double damage on an active Peragus Droid Shield and cancel it with a single use (but do no further damage until the next use), but the Shock Arm is completely unaffected.

Sealed Door
There's a sealed door in the right wall of the storage room:

 Someone has purposely welded this door shut. You'll need to blast it open with explosives.

T3-M4 can use one of the s from the corpse down in the  to blast it open, revealing a security cargo room. Otherwise, after using the  to access remote camera controls and seeing the Astromech droid 3C-FD in this room, you could attempt to overload 3C-FD's motivator by remote: this opens the door, but it also destroys 3C-FD and the plasteel cylinder by the bottom wall, and another cylinder in the top left corner by the door, leaving only a footlocker by the back right wall.

 [This utility droid looks as if it has suffered irreparable damage.]

Hangar Control Terminal
There's a low security door in the bottom wall of the storage room:

When you enter, the camera pans upward so you see the Ebon Hawk in the hangar below the control terminal's windows, which are at the top of the ramp in front of T3-M4:

There's a hangar bay door in the wall to either side of the ramp:

 This emergency blast door is magnetically sealed, and no amount of security or explosives will open it. You'll need to override it from a console.

Hangar control is at the top of the ramp, with a footlocker beneath the windows to either side:

The missing  can be replaced with those taken from the second broken droid down in the :

Once you've replaced the missing parts:

|}

|}

Down the ramp, the hangar bay door in the left wall is now open, allowing access to the . Otherwise:

|}

|}

|}

|}

If you haven't already blasted open the  in the storage room's right wall:

This opens the door but destroys 3C-FD and two plasteel cylinders, which only leaves a single footlocker inside.

Fuel Depot
Once T3-M4 has replaced the missing parts in the , you can use it to open the hangar bay door in hangar control's left wall. The corridor beyond curves around the hangar bay, where the Ebon Hawk can be seen through the windows to your left. This corridor contains three Mark I mining droids, like those encountered on the way down to the .

Beyond the door at the bottom left end is a room containing a broken droid:

Beyond the door in the left wall is a short corridor containing two more Mark I mining droids, with a footlocker in its bottom right corner by the door:

The turbolift to the fuel depot is beyond the door at the left end of the corridor.

center|thumb|320px|Map of the fuel depot accessible to T3-M4

Hangar Bay Sub-Level
The turbolift from the hangar bay takes you to the end of a walkway on the bottom right side of the fuel depot. Below you to your right is the , a maintenance level that can only be accessed by returning to the hangar bay and its storage room, then going down to the hangar's own sub-level.

Hangar Bay
The walkway away from the turbolift from the hangar bay, on the bottom right side of the fuel depot, has a containment field in its bottom wall, to your left:

 This containment field blocks access to the fuel lines below. There seems to be no way to open it.

There's a junction at the left end of this walkway.

Hangar Containment Fields
The walkway to your right at the junction leads up to three containment fields, which block the way around the corner to the left:

 This force field cuts the fuel depot off from the hangar bay, but you don't see anyway to open it or get around it.

Fuel Control Station
The walkway to your left at the junction leads down to the fuel control station:

|}

As T3 logs out after opening the emergency hatch, he's attacked from off-screen!

There's a medical supplies container by the facility's top left wall, which can be opened using the terminal to its left if you're unwilling or unable to open it any other way:

 Medical supplies taken from the medical unit in Residential Module 082 West.

Medical supplies are only received if, once you deliver the replacement , you've investigated  and you're now retrieving these medical supplies for Samhan Dobo's  operation.

As you exit into reception with the medical supplies, a TSF officer enters the facility:

Otherwise:

|}

You can now deliver the medical supplies to Samhan Dobo.

Arms Dealing
There's a communications terminal in the medical facility's top right corner:

If you deliver the replacement  to Czerka Corporation and agree to work for Jana Lorso, then Luxa of the :

 is at the right end of Residential 082 East, where you can now enter Apartment B3 for .

There's a  in the bottom right corner of the medical facility.
