title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Lower City Apartments (East)
text:
You don't need to enter the east apartments in the Lower City, but if you do and you want to return to hideout or change party selection, you'll need to return to the Lower City.

However, you can repair a sentry droid to earn experience and help combat all the Black Vulkars within (including a  and enforcer in the northwest apartment), and you can find Matrik in the southeast apartment and subsequently collect his bounty whether or not his death is real, or faked (which moves you closer to the light side of the Force). There's also a  in the northeast apartment that's well worth opening...

Lower City
The Lower City apartments have a similar layout to the south apartments, with five apartments on the outer wall of an apartment complex ring and the elevator to the ../Lower City/ on the south side.

You'll see a sentry droid in need of repair to the left of the elevator, outside the door to the southwest apartment:

|}

 The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

The sentry droid's patrol takes it clockwise around the apartment complex ring, opening all occupied apartments it passes and engaging any Black Vulkars it encounters. Unfortunately it isn't powerful enough to clear the apartment complex ring single-handed, but it can provide backup or a distraction if you need it.

The southwest apartment contains a Black Vulkar, with a footlocker against its northwest wall:

The west apartment contains two Black Vulkars, with a footlocker in its southwest corner:

Three groups of 2-3 Black Vulkars appear around the apartment complex ring: one just to the north of the southwest apartment, one to the north of the west apartment and one to the north of the northwest apartment containing the . These groups may contain up to any three of the following:

The number in each group depends on your character level, and that of your party: when character level > 6, three Black Vulkars always appear in each group. When each group appears depends on the direction you travel around the apartment complex ring: when you travel clockwise, only the groups by the southwest and west apartments appear until you make your second circuit; when you travel counter-clockwise, only the group by the northwest apartment appears until you make your second circuit (or travel in the opposite direction, in either case).

Matrik's Apartment
The southeast apartment has a low security door: 

If anyone is equipping :

Otherwise, you're still not particularly welcome:

|}

If you cannot persuade him, this is the only response which doesn't result in a fight:

Matrik's Bounty
You can speak to him again and keep trying to persuade him until he tells you what sort of trouble he's in:

Alternatively, if you've already spoken to Zax in Javyar's cantina in the Lower City about the bounties:

|}

You can ask him if there's some way you could help him:

|}

A permacrete detonator can be bought from the  in the Upper City for 50 credits. Leave the lower city apartments and immediately return to hideout, then take the elevator and continue south to the store; upon returning to the south apartments you can immediately transit back to the entrance to these apartments. Before you give Matrik the detonator, be sure to search the footlocker in his apartment.

|}

|}

Alternatively, you can try to get some of the credits you spent on it back:

|}

Refusing to give him the detonator, or any of the following responses, will result in a fight:

|}

Matrik's  has : Resist 20/- vs. Cold and Fire.

Whether Matrik's death is real or fake, you can go to Zax in Javyar's cantina in the ../Lower City/ to collect the bounty.

Security Crate
Opening the apartment door to the northeast reveals a security crate in the middle of the room with six hologram projectors arranged in a semi-circle on the floor behind it:

If you activate a hologram incorrectly:

If you activate a second hologram incorrectly, the resulting detonation will take out everyone in the apartment. If at least one party member remains outside, those in the apartment can pick themselves up and retrieve the security crate's contents from its remains, but it's better to search the desk in the east corner for a datapad containing a draft of the aforementioned biography of The Twisted Rancor Trio:

 Guts and Glory: A Chronicle of The Amazing Story of The Twisted Rancor Trio
 By Gilthos Uksaris
 (A work in progress)

 The origins of what would eventually become the most famous band in the galaxy are surprisingly humble. The brains behind the group, manager Gilthos Uksaris, founded the Trio to earn a date with a young singer named Elinda.

 The ploy worked, and Elinda became the first member of the band. Gilthos scrambled to find musicians to back her, and signed a Bith named Ujaa to be the lead musician. Soon after that he signed Ujaa's brother Ujii to complete the trio.

 The band struggled at first. Elinda was a fantastic singer, but Ujaa wasn't much of a musician. When Elinda threatened to quit, Gilthos fired Ujaa and signed another Bith named Loopa.

 Of course this didn't go over well with Ujaa's brother, and Ujii quit. Fortunately, Loopa knew another musician named Fodo, who joined to replace Ujii.

 Led by Elinda's singing, the second incarnation of The Twisted Rancor Trio became quite popular on their home world of Taris, eventually attracting the attention of local legitimate businessman Davik Kang.

 Davik asked Gilthos to bring his group in for a command performance. Gilthos agreed, realizing this could be the band's big break.  Unfortunately, Elinda had heard certain unsubstantiated rumors about Davik Kang and his connections to the Exchange. Fearing for her life, she refused to go to his estate to perform.

 Many felt that without Elinda's singing the band would crumble. But Gilthos came up with a brilliant plan to save the group by hiring Elinda's sister, Ashana, as the new lead singer on the eve of their scheduled appearance at Davik's estate. 

 Gilthos knew he was taking a risk. If Ashana couldn't perform at Elinda's level, Davik's infamous temper could have dire consequences for the entire band. However, if Ashana could match her sister's performance then Davik was likely to sign the band to a big time touring contract.

 It was a risk, but The Twisted Rancor Trio was founded on "Guts and Glory". 

 [There are no further entries.]

|}

This should enable you to activate the holographic security system in the proper order to open the security crate:

4Loopa2Ujaa1Elinda6Ashana5Fodo3Ujii

|}

Vulkar Gang Boss
The northwest apartment contains a Vulkar gang boss and an enforcer:

The Vulkar gang boss uses an , but you may be able to damage or even kill him in the first combat round with blaster fire before he does so. Otherwise, use of melee weapons or ion blasters or rifles is advised until the shield goes down.

There's also a footlocker and supplies against the southwest wall:

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Lower City Apartments (West)
text:
You don't need to enter the west apartments in the Lower City, but if you do and you want to return to hideout or change party selection, you'll need to return to the Lower City.

However, if you enter then you have an(other) encounter with Calo Nord just inside. You combat Black Vulkars within (including a   in the southwest apartment), and you can find Selven in the northeast apartment and subsequently collect her bounty. There's also a  in the northwest apartment that's well worth opening...

Lower City
These apartments have a similar layout to the south apartments, with five apartments on the outer wall of an apartment complex ring and an elevator to the ../Lower City/ on the south side. As you enter for the first time, you see Calo Nord confronting two Rodians to your left:

|}

He draws two blasters and guns down Luugro, then the second Rodian, before turning and leaving.

The apartment complex ring is patrolled in a clockwise direction by a Vulkar enforcer and two Black Vulkars. They start on the opposite side to the elevator, and if you also travel in a clockwise direction you may never encounter them... or if you're slow, they may come up behind you:

The Vulkar enforcer uses an , but you may be able to damage or even kill him in the first combat round with blaster fire before he does so. Otherwise, use of melee weapons or ion blasters or rifles is advised until the shield goes down.

Two other groups of 2-3 Black Vulkars appear around the apartment complex ring: one just to the north of the southwest apartment, and the other to the north of the northwest apartment containing the . These groups may contain up to any three of the following:

The number in each group depends on your character level, and that of your party: when character level > 6, three Black Vulkars always appear in each group. Both groups appear when you travel clockwise, but when you travel counter-clockwise they won't appear until you make your second circuit (or travel in the opposite direction).

The southeast apartment contains a Black Vulkar, with a footlocker by the northeast wall:

The west apartment contains two Black Vulkars, with a footlocker in the southwest corner:

Selven's Apartment
The northeast apartment is locked:

A woman will challenge you upon entry:

Those are the only responses which avoid a fight. Otherwise...

Selven's Bounty
If you try to enter or speak to her again, or make any other response, she attacks you:

|}

Strangely, Selven uses both  and Master Rapid Shot (but not Improved Rapid Shot). If you were already aware of her bounty:

Otherwise, you won't know about it until you've been to the bounty office in Javyar's cantina in the ../Lower City/ and spoken to Zax about his bounties.

Sealed Strongbox
The northwest apartment has a sealed strongbox in its west corner, which is mined:

This needs to be recovered, disabled or triggered to access the sealed strongbox. There's also a desk against the southwest wall:

|}

This electronic personal message center gives you the information you need to enter the proper password responses to disable the lock of the sealed strongbox (there's no other way to do so):

|}

If you don't enter all the proper password responses:

If you make a mistake, there's nothing to stop you trying again as many times as is necessary to enter all the proper password responses (although there are 216 possible combinations):

Vulkar Gang Boss
The southwest apartment contains a Vulkar gang boss and a Black Vulkar:

The Vulkar gang boss uses an , but you may be able to damage or even kill him in the first combat round with blaster fire before he does so. Otherwise, use of melee weapons or ion blasters or rifles is advised until the shield goes down.

There are supplies in the east corner to the left of the entrance.

There's also a footlocker in an alcove in the north corner to the right of the entrance, which is mined: if you're careful, it's possible to edge around the mine without setting it off to open the footlocker.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Lower Sewers
text:
To continue the search for Bastila you need to save Zaalbar from the  to the west before Mission will lower the  to the north, allowing you to travel to the ../Upper Sewers/ beyond. You encounter rakghouls and Gamorreans throughout the sewers, but you can repair a rusted droid to earn experience and help combat those guarding Zaalbar.

You can also find the two  journals sought by Rukil back in the Undercity, one on an Outcast corpse in a room just to the northeast of the Gamorrean compound's main entrance, and another just southeast of the 's lower entrance, at the northeast end of the sewers: you should return with them to the Outcast village before going into the upper sewers.

Undercity
The path of least resistance is the north entrance from the Undercity. You'll find yourself at the bottom of a ladder at the west end of a short tunnel, with a sewer door at its east end which is mined:

You can move around to the north side if you're unwilling or unable to disable or recover it (move each party member in Solo mode to avoid accidents). Beyond the door is a small room with three rakghouls and a rakghoul fiend in its southeast corner:

All rakghouls and fiends you encounter in the lower sewers will be the same as these. Beyond the southeast sewer door is the  (which will be visible on the left when you open the door). There's a skeletal corpse to the left of the southwest sewer door next to that leading to the ladder to the Undercity: this door opens onto a tunnel which turns south and marks the east boundary of the .

Oddly, the south entrance from the Undercity takes you to the northeast end of the sewers. You'll find yourself at the bottom of a ladder at the west end of a short tunnel, with a sewer door at its east end. Beyond this is a room containing a Gamorrean raid leader and two Gamorrean raiders:

There's a corpse in the northeast corner and another sewer door in the south wall. Beyond this is a tunnel to the south which turns west and ends in a sewer door. Beyond it is a chamber with water cascading into the middle of it, and a walkway around its perimeter with four Gamorreans on its east side:

Beyond the northwest sewer door is the , while beyond the southwest sewer door is a tunnel to the junction at the south end of the tunnel along the east boundary of the Gamorrean compound.

This tunnel contains a Gamorrean patrol:

Promised Land
There's a sewer door in the east wall of the tunnel along the east boundary of the , beyond which is a room which is mined:

You can edge around this easily enough to the rusted droid within:

|}

|}

 The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

This droid is a melee fighter whose patrol takes it through the main entrance of the Gamorrean compound into the middle of the barracks beyond the Gamorrean chief's room. It will explode the mine if it's still there, and it's perfectly capable of killing all enemies it encounters on its patrol without optimization or shields, even on Difficult. However, it's advisable to provide it with ranged support as it distracts the Gamorreans.

To the left of the mine is an Outcast corpse:

 This journal is a record of the long and difficult search to find the Promised Land. It contains many half completed maps and cryptic notes, all attempting to decipher whether the legend is true or simply a child's fable. By itself this journal does not contain enough information to solve the mystery, however it could be a valuable piece of the puzzle.

In the east wall of the tunnel running south from the northeast entrance from the Undercity is a sewer door, beyond which is an empty room with another sewer door at its east end. Beyond this is a room containing three rakghouls and a rakghoul fiend:

Afterwards do not return to hideout to heal, as when you transit back these rakghouls can reappear. There's also a skeletal corpse and another Outcast corpse:

You can return to the Undercity and Rukil in the Outcast village.

Gamorrean Compound
The tunnel along the east boundary of the Gamorrean compound contains another Gamorrean patrol.

The main entrance to the Gamorrean compound is through a sewer door in the west wall. Beyond it is a room with the Gamorrean chief in its northwest corner and a Gamorrean elite in each of the three remaining corners:

The Gamorrean chief has Awareness rank 50, so  is not an option.

Like all enemies in the lower sewers they're melee fighters, so it's advisable to place someone or something in the doorway to create a bottleneck, preventing them all from attacking at the same time. If neither you nor any of your ../Party/ are robust enough for this, you can activate the rusted droid in the room beyond the east sewer door opposite the main entrance: engaging its patrol mode makes it go through the main entrance and into the barracks beyond, engaging any enemies it encounters in melee combat.

Beyond the west sewer door is a barracks, containing two Gamorreans that may open this door themselves:

There's a locked weapons locker in the southeast corner of this barracks:

However, if Mission is in your party then she opens the locked door in the south wall of the previous room to free Zaalbar before you can enter the barracks beyond. Otherwise:

 [This ancient door is sealed with a manual lock, rendering security spikes useless. You will have to find someone with the right tools to open it for you.]

Search for Bastila

|}

Rancor in the Sewers

|}

You can now add Zaalbar to your party, at the expense of either Carth or Mission... but since Mission is required to lower the  preventing you from continuing to the upper sewers, it's between him and Carth.

The Gamorrean compound also has a back entrance. Continue down the tunnel along the east boundary of the compound to the sewer door at its south end. Beyond this is a junction, with a central pillar blocking the view of four rakghouls and a rakghoul fiend on its south side:

Afterwards do not return to hideout to heal, as when you transit back these rakghouls can reappear. There's a skeletal corpse at the bottom of the ladder at the end of the cul-de-sac beyond the south sewer door.

 The exit at the top of the ladder seems to be blocked with no way to clear it.

Beyond the west sewer door is a tunnel to the waterfall mentioned earlier; beyond the southwest sewer door is a short tunnel which is mined:

This can be passed on the north side without it exploding. The sewer door at the end of this tunnel opens to reveal a second chamber with water cascading into the middle of it, and a walkway around its perimeter with three rakghouls and a rakghoul fiend on it:

Again, these may reappear after leaving and returning to the area. Beyond the south sewer door is another cul-de-sac with a corpse at the end of it. Beyond the northwest door is a tunnel which turns north along the west boundary of the Gamorrean compound.

Beyond the sewer door in the east wall of this tunnel is another short tunnel ending in a malfunctioning sewer door, through the cracks of which you may just see Zaalbar imprisoned. Beyond the sewer door at the north end of the tunnel is a room containing two rakghouls and a rakghoul fiend:

In the northwest corner are a corpse and skeletal corpse. The sewer door in the west wall is mined:

This can just about be edged around if you walk. The door is also locked:

Beyond is the barracks behind the Gamorrean chief's room mentioned earlier.

Force Field
After rescuing Zaalbar from the , exit it through its main entrance to the east and go north up the tunnel along its east boundary, then through the southeast sewer door in the room at its end. Beyond is a short tunnel ending in another sewer door. Both doors are mined:

You can just about edge around these if you pass them on the northeast side. You'll see the force field in the northeast wall, and force field control against the opposite wall.

If you access it without Mission in your party before saving Zaalbar, or with her before saving him:

|}

So you need to access it with Mission in your party after saving Zaalbar:

Once the shield is lowered you can enter the upper sewers beyond it.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Lower Shadowlands
text:
The  from the  is at the north end of the Lower Shadowlands. You only need to get the Star Map from the  to the southwest, avoiding the  with an armed party leader, even if you find their  to the west: once you have the map, you can continue the  and leave the Shadowlands, and Kashyyyk.

You don't need to help the  unless you want Zaalbar back, and once you have him it's the only reason to come here more than once.  can be found to the east then north: you can simply kill him to side with Chuundar, moving closer to the dark side of the Force, but if you found the  in the Upper Shadowlands then you should return to the village's  beforehand.

You can keep your options open a little longer by returning from the  to the southeast with Bacca's blade for Freyyr but, once you leave the Shadowlands, if you don't side with Chuundar then you must side with Freyyr, moving closer to the light side of the Force: if you found the broken droid in the Upper Shadowlands then you need to return to port beforehand to complete .

Upper Shadowlands
The  from the Upper Shadowlands is in a clearing at the north end of the Lower Shadowlands. A path exits the clearing to the southwest, turning south and ending at an intersection where three Wookiee corpses lie slain and the only remaining survivor, Grrrwahrr, duels one Mandalorian while two others watch:

Grrrwahrr kills the Mandalorian, and the other two now engage him in combat. You can help him with the , although he's invulnerable and may kill them both all by himself while the rest of the Shadowlands are explored (although all remaining Mandalorians can be sought and destroyed as you travel towards the Star Map to the southwest).

Star Map: Kashyyyk

If you take the southeast path and encounter , the Wookiee that Chuundar sent you to kill, before acquiring the Star Map, he can point you in the right direction if you spare him long enough to return and ask him about it:

He means you should go up the path to the northwest, then take the only remaining path into the lower Shadowlands at the intersection where Grrrwahrr fights the Mandalorians, to the southwest. Continuing southwest beyond another intersection with three Wookiee corpses and a clearing to the northwest, you'll encounter viper kinraths, the number of which depends on your character level:

 Character level < 16 16 > 16 Viper Kinraths 3 5 6

You or any level > 8 Jedi in your party should use Improved  or Knight or Master Valor to give your party Immunity: .

Unless otherwise indicated, all other viper kinraths encountered in the lower Shadowlands are identical to these. 

Take the southeast path to another intersection with three Wookiee corpses, where you'll see a dead end to the southeast and another intersection to the southwest. To the south are paths to the southwest and southeast, both of which lead to the Star Map.

Computer
The computer hologram by the Star Map can actually be seen in the distance down the southeast path. As you approach it from the left, you'll find it's mined:

The southwest path first leads to a clearing, with a path to the southeast approaching the computer hologram from the right.

center|thumb|640px|The computer hologram, with the Star Map behind it to the right, as seen from the path approaching it from the right.

This approach is also mined:

The Star Map is to the right of the computer hologram:

 [The Star Map is sealed and cannot be opened.]

The only option is to talk to the computer. You can ask it questions:

You can ask what it means by behavioral reconfiguration:

You can ask questions about it and this installation:

You can ask what limitations have been placed on its programming:

|}

However, it's only necessary to say you're seeking information about a Star Map, and what you need to do to get access to it, before beginning an evaluation:

|}

The evaluation consists of three questions, beginning with the following:

|}

While trusting Zaalbar is the wrong answer, the right answer moves you closer to the dark side of the Force:

|}

The following responses end the evaluation prematurely, with violence:

However, it's best to continue the evaluation to move closer to the light or dark side of the Force:

Otherwise:

|}

Even a light side character should not give the following response, as it ends the evaluation prematurely:

|}

Preparing your forces to attack in ten days but doing nothing in the city is the correct answer, and you can move closer to the light or dark side of the Force depending on the logic of your decision:

|}

Answering the third and final question will also move you closer to the light or dark side of the Force:

|}

If you answer the final question correctly, you move closer to the dark side of the Force, and the Star Map is yours:

|}

Otherwise, two defense droids approach from the northwest to engage you in combat. They receive bonuses depending on your character level:

 Character level Dexterity Vitality 12-14 +6  +60 > 14 +10  +100

Thus at character level > 14:

Both droids use their  (which makes them immune to Force Whirlwind as long as it's active) and their special weapons and grenades whenever possible. However, Jolee must be a member of your party at this time and he has Disable Droid even if you don't, which should make killing them a lot easier.

Due to the experience received, even a dark side character may want to threaten to take it apart to get the Star Map rather than answering the last question. Once the droids are killed, the Star Map is yours:

Regardless of how the Star Map was acquired:

|}

 You have recorded the coordinates from the Star Map you found on Kashyyyk into a datapad.

Quest for the Star Forge

Chieftain in Need

Take the southeast path from the first intersection to the south of the entrance from the . It winds until you reach an intersection where you'll encounter viper kinraths, the number of which depends on your character level:

 Character level < 16 16 > 16 Viper Kinraths 3 5 6

You or any level > 8 Jedi in your party should use Improved  or Knight or Master Valor to give your party Immunity: .

Down the south path from the intersection you'll see more viper kinraths at the corner to the west:

You'll also encounter more if you continue east until the path ends in a clearing to the southeast:

A path to the northeast is a dead end, down which you can see a lone Wookiee...

Freyyr
When you speak to the lone Wookiee, Freyyr, he first attacks you:

Although Jolee must be a member of your party at this time, if he isn't nearby:

|}

He receives bonuses depending on your character level:

 Character level Strength Dexterity Vitality 12-14 +4  +4  +50 > 14 +6  +6  +100

Thus at character level > 14:

After being reduced to 25% vitality or less (although it's closer to 30% at level > 12), combat ends and he speaks again:

If you're in Solo mode and none of your party are nearby, this is your first opportunity to kill him, moving (much) closer to the dark side of the Force:

He heals 75 vitality but loses any bonuses depending on your character level before continuing to fight to the death.

When you return to the  in the upper Shadowlands, Gorwooken takes you directly to Chuundar:

|}

However, once you've killed Freyyr you'll receive no experience for recovering Bacca's blade after killing the ritual beast. Furthermore, although you'll move slightly closer to the dark side of the Force if you kill him here, you'll engage in much more combat and thus receive much more experience if you return Bacca's blade to him now but side with Chuundar later.

Otherwise, Jolee objects (and does so upon every response to kill Freyyr), or Bastila or Juhani will do so if he isn't nearby. However, the objections can always be overruled...

Otherwise:

Otherwise:

Otherwise:

|}

You can speak to him again about the Mandalorians, the Star Map if you haven't already acquired it (or the  if you have), or you can still decide to kill him for Chuundar:

|}

Once you have Bacca's Sword Blade after killing the ritual beast, it can be returned to him:

Otherwise:

|}

When you return to the basket up in the upper Shadowlands, Gorwooken and two hidden Wookiees attack you:

They receive bonuses depending on your character level:

 Character level Strength Dexterity Vitality 12-14 +4  +4  +50 > 14 +6  +6  +100

Thus at character level > 14:

Gorwooken has Immunity: ... which is just as well, since the two Wookiees can use up to four s each. Any level > 8 Jedi in your party can use Improved  or Knight or Master Valor to give your party Immunity: Poison as well.

From now on, you'll use the basket yourself:

Back up on the Great Walkway, Chorrawl speaks as you approach him again, before taking you back to the ../Hall of the Chieftain/ to choose between Freyyr and Chuundar:

|}

Ritual Marker
Take the path to the west then south of  and follow it around the corner to the west until you reach a crossroads. Across to the southwest is a dead end containing three viper kinraths:

You or any level > 8 Jedi in your party should use Improved  or Knight or Master Valor to give your party Immunity: .

 The corpse of an exceptionally large viper kinrath, freshly killed.

If you've already spoken to Freyyr about Bacca's blade:

At the crossroads take the southeast path, which goes east before turning south and ending in a large clearing with a ritual marker and a dangling vine in its northeast corner:

Follow these instructions using the dangling vine, and the Ritual Beast will appear:

If you return with Zaalbar after killing Freyyr and reporting back to Chuundar:

Otherwise:

Otherwise:

|}

The ritual beast appears to the north, cutting off the exit to the clearing:

You or any level > 8 Jedi in your party should use Improved  or Knight or Master Valor to give your party Immunity: . It in turn is immune to Force Push and Whirlwind and cannot be knocked back and down, but Force Wave can still damage and stun it. Conversely, its own Slam Attack can be a nuisance for melee attackers, knocking them back and down even when they save against it.

|}

 This is part of Bacca's Ceremonial Blade, damaged due to the arrogance of Chieftain Rothrrrawr. He underestimated a creature in the Shadowlands (later dubbed the Great Beast), and lost the blade in its hide. The hilt remained in his court, passed to other chieftains. If both pieces could be found, the sword might be able to be reassembled.

No experience is received for recovering Bacca's blade if  has already been killed. Bacca's blade can be returned to Freyyr, or if he's been killed then it can be returned to Chuundar. If you return with Zaalbar after killing Freyyr and reporting back to Chuundar:

|}

Otherwise, you only receive Bacca's Sword Blade.

 This data pad was recovered from the remains of a terentatek on Kashyyyk, and must have been devoured by the beast. It appears to be the personal journal of Guun Han Saresh. The last entry explains what he was doing on Kashyyyk:

 Duran and Shaela have given in to their passion for each other, and are doomed to fall to the dark side. I tried to warn them against expressing their love, but they called me arrogant and accused me - ME! - of being the one on the dark path. I left the fools on Korriban.

 But I am not about to abandon the mandate given me by the Jedi Council. I will destroy the terentatek wherever I find them. I have heard rumors such a beast may exist in the Shadowlands of Kashyyyk.

 I shall go there and slay the beast, proving that I do not need either Duran or Shaela with me to defeat these creatures!

|}

Deesra may have warned you about the terentatek and told you about the Great Hunt for them before leaving Dantooine, and now that you've encountered one you may return to tell him about it. As you might expect, the remainder are to be found on ../Korriban/...

Hidden Hunters
Once Grrrwahrr has killed the first Mandalorian, you can search his remains:

Grrrwahrr is invulnerable so he'll eventually kill the two remaining without help, but it's much quicker to join in:

../Medical items/ are only received if unused. Grrrwahrr speaks to you:

Refuse to help to move closer to the dark side of the Force:

If Zaalbar is present, he insists that you help him:

Otherwise, you can avoid moving closer to ether side of the Force by telling him you can't help:

|}

Alternatively, you can give him a medpac to move closer to the light side of the Force and continue the dialog:

He runs north to leave the lower Shadowlands. Otherwise:

|}

This quest can also be activated and completed without healing him, but you won't receive experience or a reward from him for doing so.

Only the party leader needs to be unarmed for the hidden hunters to reveal themselves, and once they do so a weapon can be equipped again. There are two groups of three Mandalorians waiting in ambush to the south: there's a clearing containing three fallen Wookiees just down the southwest path; continue southwest beyond and then down the southeast path to the other.

The first ambush you encounter, regardless of location, consists of the following:

This Mandalorian to the west may use grenades, and like that to the east has : Resist 25/- vs. Sonic, while that to the north has Immunity: . The latter two receive bonuses depending on your character level:

 Character level Strength Dexterity Vitality 12-14 +4  +4  +50 > 14 +6  +6  +100

Thus at character level > 14:

 This request is in the Mandalorian language. "A stump disabled the stabilizers on my swoop. I request parts before other systems fail. If the generator goes, my blending field will stop working and I'll be visible to our prey."

|}

 This is a personal log in the Mandalorian language. "This hunt is no challenge. How will attacking unarmed creatures train us to use these Jedi toys? You want new warriors to learn? Watching a comrade lop his own arm off fighting a real opponent would teach more than these pointless battles. I obey, Mandalore, but with protest. The blending field generators on the swoops grant near perfect camouflage. Why only attack unarmed opponents?"

|}

The second ambush you encounter consists of the following:

This Mandalorian to the north has Immunity: Mind-Affecting, and may use grenades. The others to the east and west are identical to those in the previous ambush.

 This device attaches to a swoop bike, transmitting any field data that has been collected on it to the Commander.

Swoop Bikes
Once both Mandalorian ambushes have been sprung and you have the swoop bike signal device, follow the paths to the west to a clearing lined by three Mandalorian swoop bikes. Those on the north and east sides can be ignored.

 [The Swoop Bike is still warm to the touch. There is a Signal Device on it, however, it contains no field data to transmit.]

Placing the signal device in the swoop bike on the southwest side will cause the Mandalorian commander to appear behind you with the last two of his subordinates.

|}

The Mandalorian on the left is identical to those to the west in the first two ambushes. The Mandalorian commander himself has Immunity:  and : Resist 25/- vs. Electrical, and may use up to three s. He and the remaining Mandalorian on the right receive bonuses depending on your character level:

 Character level Strength Dexterity Vitality 12-14 +4  +4  +50 > 14 +6  +6  +100

Thus at character level > 14:

 This is the helmet of a fierce Mandalorian warrior, taken from a group that stalked the Shadowlands of Kashyyyk for wounded or unwary prey.

Return the helmet to Grrrwahrr to receive more experience and a reward (this requires you to heal him if you haven't already done so, moving closer to the light side of the Force):

Otherwise:

|}

He runs north to leave the lower Shadowlands.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Matale Grounds
text:
To complete the , all you need to do is cross the Matale grounds from a  from the plains outside the courtyard to a  to the grove.

Aside from kath hounds and horned kath hounds, there's a Mandalorian and three Duros warriors at the west end of the grounds and, once you've spoken to Hulas on Manaan about proving yourself worthy of the ../Genoharadan/, Zuulan Sentar can be found at the northeast corner of the  in the middle of the grounds. 

Path North
There are two paths north, one at the west end of the Matale grounds and the other at the east end, which lead to the respective ends of the courtyard.

At the east end there's a horn kath hound and two kath hounds to the west of the path north, beyond which is the approach to the east side of the Matale estate.

Should you try to sneak past them by hugging the north wall, you'll encounter another kath hound lying at the base of a tree.

Mandalorian Raiders
At the west end of the Matale grounds there are two landspeeders to the east where a Mandalorian, accompanied by three Duros warriors, threatens a farmer as you approach:

The Mandalorian guns down this "hero".

If he's the first Mandalorian you kill:

Although the Mandalorian is the primary target, his Duros allies are considerably weaker so picking them off before focusing on him is advisable.

There's an equipment pack by the back of the nearest landspeeder.

Continue east then turn south to cross a bridge over a river which forms the west boundary of the Matale estate.

Matale Estate
The Matale estate is in the center of the Matale grounds, with doors in its north and west walls. If you try to open either door, you'll find it locked.

 [Matale passcard required to enter.]

You can talk briefly to the Matale droid guarding the west door to the left.

|}

There's a horn kath hound wandering the east approach to the estate.

Another appears if you leave then return to the area.

Genoharadan: Zuulan
After speaking to Hulas in Ahto City's East Central courtyard on Manaan and telling him you're ready to prove yourself worthy of the Genoharadan, you'll find Zuulan's speeder parked at the northeast corner of the Matale estate.

After your party hides behind rocks to the east, Zuulan and two guard droids approach from the west and all are killed in the blast. However, since no experience is received and this costs you a frag mine, it's better to slice into the speeder and activate its alarm system to bring them running:

|}

If you try to interact with Zuulan's speeder again:

 [Now that you've dealt with Zuulan, you have no further use for his speeder.]

Damage inflicted by Shock or Force Lightning or Storm can be significantly reduced, or even negated entirely.

All three are ranged attackers grouped close enough together for all to be within the area of effect of grenades. Once Zuulan has been reduced to 20% Vitality or his two droids have been killed, he disengages from combat and begs you not to kill him, offering to pay you to let him live:

|}

This may allow a light side character to get something out of this quest without moving closer to the dark side of the Force, but the reward is much greater if you don't spare him:

Regardless of how he's killed:

Return to Hulas in Ahto City's East Central courtyard on Manaan to (try to) collect his bounty.

Path South
There are two paths south, one at the west end of the Matale grounds and the other at the east end, which lead to the respective ends of the grove.

The west path south is up the slope to the south, to the west of the Mandalorian raider. You can travel there from the west path north from the courtyard without any hostile contact.

The east path south is on the other side of a plain on which a horn kath hound wanders.

Another appears if you leave then return to the area. On the east side of this plain are two level 3 kath hounds.

In the southwest corner of the plain are three kath hounds, the closest of which in the center is level 6, while the other two are level 3.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Medical items
text:
Medical items are all Single Use. Medpacs heal living beings while repair kits allow droids to repair themselves. Only one can be used per round once engaged in combat (unless a shield or stimulant has already been used in that round), although there's no restriction when this isn't the case. They're normally only received from enemies killed if they weren't used beforehand.

The cost of Antidote Kits and all medpacs may treble after acquiring the Star Map on Manaan depending on how this was achieved. In this event, they can be sold on the ../Yavin Station/ afterwards for almost twice what they cost to buy beforehand (100*3 * 65/100 = 195%).

Once  join your party and you become one yourself, the light side powers  and Heal can heal all organic members of your party within a 15 meter radius both during and after combat, while the dark side powers  and Death Field allow the user to heal during combat. However, medpacs are still useful when one character suffers particularly heavy damage or Force points need to be conserved during prolonged combat.

If you speak to Jolee in Medical on the Ebon Hawk after he's joined your party in the Upper Shadowlands of Kashyyyk, then you can ask him to make a healing kit for you: he'll make Advanced Medpacs if you're character level < 11, and Life Support Packs thereafter. title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Mines
text:
All mines have Area of Effect: 3.3m radius. Hostile mines can normally be detected with a successful  skill check, then simply avoided, or disabled with a successful  skill check.

Lesser Demolitions skill is required to set your own mines. Although many mines can be bought or found in containers, many more, particularly the most damaging and effective Deadly mines (which can never be bought), are only available with greater Demolitions skill to allow recovery of hostile mines for your own use.

Maximum 15 mines can be set in the same area. Mines are best set when anticipating combat with melee attackers who can be lured back to trigger them. However, due to the limited supply of Average and Deadly mines, and the time spent setting them and then luring enemies, they're best used sparingly unless playing solo or confronted by one or two really tough opponents.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/North Apartments
text:
After entering from ../Upper City North/, you need to get the Sith Armor so that you can return and fool the Sith guarding the Upper City elevator to gain access to the Lower City: if you haven't been invited to a party in Upper City South's cantina, then you receive this from the remains of the Sith commander in the northwest apartment; otherwise, you can get it from a Sith backpack in the west apartment if male, or the northeast apartment if female.

 is to the southeast, where you can complete  and move much closer to the light side of the Force by paying his debt (200 credits!), or closer to the dark side of the Force by extorting and killing him (this is also possible without affecting your alignment, but may feel out of character if light side).

Upper City
These apartments have a similar layout to the ../South Apartments/, with five apartments on the outer wall of an apartment complex ring and an elevator back to the Upper City in the outer wall on the south side. The ring is populated by a maintenance droid, a child, two women and a man, all of whom will comment when spoken to but none of whom can be engaged in dialog:

 Beep beep beep-oop!

 Is you one of the Sith? My daddy says the Sith are nothing but bullies. You don't look like a bully. My Momma says I have to stay out of the Lower City. That's where bad people live. You ever seen a swoop bike? I seen them at the races sometimes. They go fast and make lots of noise! You're one of them Sith, ain't you? My mommy says I'm not supposed to talk to you.

|}

 Taris used to be a nice place, before the Sith showed up and started bossing us around! Stay out of the Lower City. That place is overrun with gangs! I wonder if any of those Republic space pods survived crash landing in the Undercity? I'm... I'm sorry. I don't want to get in the way of official Sith business.

|}

 I've got a ton of things to do today. I can't talk to you. I heard the gangs have overrun the Lower City. Why don't the Sith go down there and restore order? I heard the Sith are sending salvage teams down into the Undercity to recover those Republic escape pods. Please, don't take me in for questioning... I don't know anything! I swear!

|}

All five apartments contain a footlocker, although those to the southwest and southeast have low security doors:

The southeast apartment is  and the southwest apartment contains a family of a man, woman and child, who will comment if you speak to them but won't engage you in dialog:

 Woman Child Man I remember when a person didn't have to worry about thieves rummaging through their home! You ain't supposed to be here! This ain't your home! Don't – don't hurt my family! Just take what you want and get out. I'm... I'm sorry. I don't want to get in the way of official Sith business. You're one of them Sith, ain't you? My mommy says I'm not supposed to talk to you. Please, don't take me in for questioning... I don't know anything! I swear!

Search for Bastila
If you've come here directly without being invited to a party by an off-duty Sith in Upper City South's cantina, then travel from the elevator to the northwest apartment, outside which a Sith trooper is standing guard. This is the recommended option, since it gives you the chance to receive more experience and more items, and possibly move closer to the light or dark side of the Force. If you don't speak to the Sith trooper, as you pass he speaks to you:

Within the northwest apartment, an alien prisoner standing in the north corner is being interrogated by the Sith commander, while another Sith trooper searches the footlocker in the west corner:

|}

If you get involved, you fight all three Sith now. Otherwise:

|}

The Sith commander guns down the alien prisoner, then issues a command to the Sith trooper standing outside:

The Sith trooper goes inside to start searching the east corner of the room. If you follow him, he challenges you:

|}

Now you have to fight all three Sith anyway:

 This full body armor could be used to fool people into thinking the wearer was one of the Sith.

You can equip this to fool the guard at the Upper City elevator, giving you access to the Lower City.

If you got involved before the alien prisoner was killed, you can speak to him now:

|}

If you speak to him after anyone has equipped Sith Armor:

|}

 

Otherwise, if Carth isn't present:

Invited to a Party
If you have been invited to a party by an off-duty Sith in Upper City South's cantina, your destination will depend on your sex: if you're male, you were invited by Sarna, who lives in the west apartment; if you're female, you were invited by Yun Genda, who lives in the northeast apartment. The only other difference is who speaks to you and your host:

|}

 This full body armor could be used to fool people into thinking the wearer was one of the Sith.

You can equip this to fool the guard at the Upper City elevator, giving you access to the Lower City.

Largo's Apartment
Largo lives in the southeast apartment with a low security door:
 

Otherwise:

|}

Otherwise, if you want the credits he offers but don't want to move closer to the dark side of the Force, end the dialog without killing him and then return:

Largo's Bounty
Even if you've extorted credits from Largo, you can still offer to help him:

If you have at least 200 credits:

Although you may move much closer to the light side of the Force and gain some experience, 200 credits is a significant sum at this point in the game and unfortunately for Largo, the rewards for killing him are significantly higher.

Even more unfortunately for Largo, you can kill him without moving closer to the dark side of the Force by ending the dialog without killing him and returning to extort credits from him a second time:

You'll also receive 50 credits if you haven't already done so, and you can go to Zax in Javyar's cantina in the Lower City to collect the bounty.

Alternatively, you can end the dialog without killing him and give yourself some time to decide whether you should do so:

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/North Beach
text:
You enter the  from the  at its south end. If you already left the ../Elder Settlement/ peacefully, then those on this beach and in the  on its northeast side are hostile, or they can become so if you are hostile.

Otherwise, after being taken to the One and leaving this settlement peacefully, you can go to Warleader Garn in the northwest corner of the beach to be told about the  lying in wait outside the Temple, and return here after the leader is slain to claim your reward.

Central Beach
The path back to the central beach is behind you to the south. The path ahead leads north, then northwest and northeast before you emerge at the southwest corner of the north beach, where you'll see the sea to the north and a settlement to the northeast. However, before you can step onto the beach you'll be challenged by a Rakatan elite warrior accompanied by three Rakatan warriors and two young rancors. If you've already left the ../Elder Settlement/ on the south beach peacefully then combat is inevitable:

Otherwise:

|}

You're taken to the arena of the One within the Rakatan settlement to the northeast: this is recommended regardless of your character's alignment or need to gain experience. Otherwise, they engage in melee combat:

|}

The warriors use a ,  and :

Debilitating their two war beasts is advisable due to the strength of their melee attacks: although they're immune to Force Push and Whirlwind and cannot be knocked back and down, Force Wave can still damage and stun them.

Regardless of how you enter the Rakatan settlement, once inside you cannot return to Ebon Hawk or change party selection without exiting.

Rakatan Settlement
The settlement entrance is on the northeast side of the beach: if you enter after engaging in combat on the beach, it will be hostile. Otherwise, upon exiting peacefully after being taken to the One, two young rancors wander the beach, as do five Rakata, three of whom use a  while the two remaining use a :

 Once the Red Rakata are destroyed there will be none who dare to stand against our tribe! We are the greatest of the Black Rakata. No leader is stronger than the One, and no other tribe commands the war beasts as we do. The One is the greatest warrior in the long history of our tribe. He will lead us to victory over all our enemies! The One is studying the secrets of the Red Rakata. In time he will use them to unlock the knowledge trapped within the Temple of the Ancients!

|}

 The technology of the Red Rakata is a powerful weapon. It even allows their tribe to stand against the might of our war beasts. It was the One who found and trained our great war beasts. Because of them, none will dare stand against our tribe. Few among us expected you to ever return, Revan. Yet the One understood you would not abandon us. With the knowledge of the Red Rakata the One will lead us to dominance over all the other tribes of the world!

|}

Should they be(come) hostile then those using a vibroblade are the same as the Rakata warriors first encountered except they only have  rank 4, not 7, while those using a quarterstaff are s:

Warleader Garn is the same as the Rakatan elite warrior first encountered in all but name.

Invisible Mandalorians
Warleader Garn stands in the northwest corner of the beach:

|}

|}

 will ambush you as you approach the single pillar standing to the southeast of the temple exterior, even if this quest hasn't been activated. Once you've killed their captain and retrieved the head from his remains, you can return to claim your reward:

|}

He leads you to a footlocker in the surf behind some rocks in the northwest corner of the beach, and unlocks it before leaving:

Although his departure means you cannot subsequently kill him, more experience should always be received for completing this quest.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Party
text:
In most areas you can use the PARTY SELECTION screen to quickly switch party members in and out as you need them. This is done instantly and without having to return to your base. Characters switched out of your party will wait for you back at your base. Remember: any equipped items will remain on the character, so these items will not show up in your inventory when a character is removed from the party. You will have to add the character to your party again if you want access to their equipped items.

32px Carth

Carth must be a member of your party before you leave your  for the first time on Taris.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Pazaak
text:
Pazaak is a card game resembling Blackjack. Playing is optional, but it can be a good way to get credits (particularly for light side characters) and some other rewards.

Pazaak Rules
This is activated when you acquire a Pazaak deck from one of the following characters:

 World Area Source Cost  Force Taris Upper City Cantina Garouk 50     Dantooine Jedi Enclave  100     Tatooine Cantina  100     Kashyyyk Czerka Landing Port Fodo Medoo 75 0   Manaan West Central Jolan Aphett 200     Ahto West Gonto Yas 100     Yavin Yavin Station  100    

Since some characters can be persuaded using skill or the Force to give you a Pazaak deck for free, there's no real need to buy one on Taris (50 credits may be a trifling sum, but so are the amounts you can wager there) unless you want to minimize travel between worlds.

This 'quest' is completed when you play a game of Pazaak for a wager, although you receive no experience for doing so. However, before wagering you should really acquire better cards for your side deck, since the only available cards from which to choose initially are two of each from +1 to +5:

 This is a standard Pazaak deck, complete with side deck cards. Card +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6 Amount                    

Obviously and ideally, you want a side deck of ten +/- cards, some of which can be bought from merchants:

 Pazaak requires both a main deck and a side deck. You can store all your side deck cards here and bring them out when you start a game.

 This is a standard Pazaak side deck card, for use with a Pazaak deck. Card +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6 Cost                                 

+/- Cards are obviously more useful than purely positive or negative cards and thus cost more credits, but cost doesn't always indicate usefulness: for example, negative cards are normally more useful than positive cards since you don't start with them, but they can be used to avoid a bust before you end turn, forcing your opponent to take another turn and draw another card, thus making it more likely that your opponent goes bust or has to use a card to avoid it (this is particularly true since you always draw first, starting at a disadvantage). Given your initial deck, you shouldn't waste credits on positive cards (with the possible exception of +6, although there are obviously much better cards).

 World Merchant +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6 Taris Uriah                            Igear                   Dantooine                                                     Tatooine                     Manaan Shady Rodian                                Korriban Mika Dorin                   

Igear sells for 25% less, Mika Dorin for 50% more (but he can only do so once you escape the Leviathan, having been brought on board after leaving the planet on which you found a fourth Star Map). Cards can also be acquired for free elsewhere (after leaving Taris, this is usually via a final wager after defeating your opponents a certain number of times):

 World Area Source +1  +2  +3 -2  -3 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±6 Taris Lower Sewers Weapons Locker           Black Vulkar Base (Garage) Garage Head's Desk         Davik's Estate Footlockers          Dantooine Jedi Enclave          Kashyyyk Czerka Landing Port          Manaan West Central           Leviathan Prison Block Contraband         

Any cards acquired before you have a Pazaak deck aren't displayed in , and afterwards they're simply added to its side deck, so you cannot sell unwanted cards.

You can replace your entire initial side deck of + cards with the equivalent +/- cards before leaving Dantooine, giving you a much better chance of winning when your opponents draw 4 random cards from the following decks:

 Deck +1  +2  +3  +4  +5  +6 -1  -2  -3  -4  -5  -6 ±1  ±2  ±3  ±4  ±5  ±6 1                                  2                                  3                                 

Unless otherwise stated, all tutorials and practice games just use deck 1. Most opponents stop playing once you've won a certain number of wagers, or switch to a higher deck as the wager increases. Final wagers aren't always for credits, and can sometimes be for Pazaak cards or another reward:

 World Opponent Maximum wager (wins)  Deck 1 Deck 2 Deck 3  Taris             Dantooine       Tatooine rowspan=2   200 (4)   Xbox     200   Kashyyyk   (4)  200 (4)   Manaan    200 (10)      200 (10)   Korriban    100 (∞)   Yavin      

Although you can normally wager for as little as a single credit, it resets to maximum at the start of each match so it's best to wager for the maximum amount. However, even after you replace your entire deck with +/- cards to match opponents using deck 3, you're still at a significant disadvantage: you always draw first from the main deck at the beginning of each set, which means you'll most likely be the first to stand, go bust or use a card, all of which make it more likely that you'll be defeated. It may be exploitative, but you can save game before playing and after winning, and load game after losing to offset this (although there's no need once the wager isn't for credits).

Once you've defeated him five more times than he's defeated you, he accuses you of cheating and will no longer play (if you play a consecutive game after this occurs then he doesn't accuse you until it has been played, regardless of the result):

|}

If you quit before wagering then this counts as a defeat while costing you nothing, which can allow you to play Niklos indefinitely. However, you can do likewise with Gelrood without needing to keep track of outcomes. The only reason to play Niklos is to unlock dialog.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Prison Block
text:
Save game if you haven't already. Once captured by the ../Leviathan/, your party member must retrieve a Sith passcard from the south , or use the central  with computer spikes or the Rodian prisoner's ICE Breaker from the southeast , to unlock the door to the west  area:

 Party Start Equipped Canderous     HK-47     Jolee     Juhani     Mission  Cell Block   T3-M4  Droid Maintenance  

The detention terminal inside can now unlock aft holding cells and equipment storage, freeing you and the rest of your party. While everyone else returns to the Ebon Hawk, you, Bastila and Carth can retrieve party inventory before taking the east  to the Bridge Command Deck to unlock its hangar and then escape.

Cell Block
Mission is stripped of her equipment and taken by a Sith guard to the southeast cell of the cell block:

He approaches her threateningly:

|}

Otherwise, Jolee is stripped of his equipment and taken to the southwest cell of the cell block:

|}

It's (far) more trouble for Jolee to let him out than to kill him, since the cell door is tougher than the guard (who's unarmed, and only has 8 Vitality):

If the Rodian prisoner in the northeast cell is approached by T3-M4:

|}

If he's approached by anyone else:

Upon returning:

|}

 rank > 13 will unlock his cell door then and there, otherwise it can be bashed or opened with the starboard cell block key, acquired from the Sith guard patrolling the corridor linking the cell block to the main corridor to the north. Mission should run across the T-junction to the west end of the cell block, ideally while his back is turned (although he normally remains in the north corridor even if he notices her), where there's a container of riot equipment by the west wall and a locked contraband container in the northwest corner:

The stealth field generator should allow her to return and  the guard:

 This keycard will unlock the cells on the Leviathan's starboard detention block.

Upon the Rodian prisoner's release:

 This device is used by criminal elements and covert operatives to slice into security computers. This particular breaker is configured for the computers on the Leviathan's brig deck. It won't work anywhere else.

You could also release the unarmed but insane Rodians from the northwest cell next door:

However, the brig terminal offers a better alternative...

Brig Terminal
Beyond the standard door in the west wall of the corridor linking the  to the south and the main corridor of the prison block to the north is a room containing the brig terminal, which can be used to open  to the west (among other things). A technician stands by it in the northeast corner close to the door, while another stands further away on the south side of the room: both draw s, switching to s in melee range. There's also a storage container in the northwest corner.

 rank > 11 is required to slice the computer and open the detention area using the 8 computer spikes acquired from this storage container and the contraband in the corridor to the southwest. However, even if this is possible it's far better to free the Rodian prisoner in the northeast cell and use the ICE breaker he gives you in return, as its 99 spikes allow you to access all system commands:

|}

As ever, accessing security cameras is an invaluable scouting tool, but accessing the cell block also gives you an opportunity to empty the cells, and the :

|}

Since no experience is received for those killed while using the computer, it's best to just release the cell force fields before logging out, allowing the three insane Rodians from the northwest cell to fight it out with the five Sith troopers from the barracks; you may then slice the computer to engage the emergency riot system to kill the survivors before logging out to receive experience for doing both.

Barracks
Beyond the standard door in the south wall at the west end of the cell block corridor is the barracks, which contains five Sith troopers with s who switch to s in melee range:

There are three lockers lining the west wall in the southwest corner, a storage box in the southeast corner, and a footlocker between the beds by the south wall:

 This appears to be a high security passcard for the detention area.

Mission could use  to sneak past the troopers to retrieve the Sith passcard, and using the  to eliminate them is another possibility.

Droid Maintenance
T3-M4 is taken to Droid Maintenance on the west side of the prison block, where he must correctly complete three number series to prevent his memory being wiped:

|}

|}

|}

|}

Failure is not an option:

 Your entire party has beenkilled.Return to main menu.

Alternatively, HK-47 simply has to kill the unarmed technician who brought him here: since he only has one Vitality, even if HK-47 had been stripped of his equipment he could still kill him with a single punch.

There's a bench of droid upgrades and a footlocker by the west wall in the southwest and northwest corners respectively:

The flame throwers should allow T3-M4 or HK-47 to make short work of any enemy in their way (save the advanced one for the Sith guard and troopers, and insane Rodians if need be). There's also a decommissioned droid in the northeast corner:

|}

 The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

It patrols the corridor between Droid Maintenance and the room containing the  to the southeast, opening the standard doors to both and engaging all enemies. The 11 parts in this room allow even a character with  rank < 4 to reactivate the droid and engage its patrol mode (and even optimize its weaponry or targeting systems), while all repairs are possible with Repair rank > 11. However, these aren't necessary as even on Difficult it can kill and not be killed in turn without optimizing its weaponry or targeting systems, or activating its .

Medical
Canderous is left alone in Medical after being stripped of his equipment, which is stored in the patient gear container in the southeast corner. There are also two large well-stocked lockers of medical supplies by the west wall in the southwest corner:

Beyond the standard door in the north wall is the main corridor, with  opposite and the T-junction leading south to the ,  and  to the east.

Detention
There are three more technicians standing at the west end of the main corridor:

The corridor turns south and then west again to the door of the detention area:

This door can be opened using the , or unlocked using the Sith passcard from the footlocker in the . Once it's open, there are locked cell doors in the west and south walls (beyond which are the energy cages holding you, Bastila and Carth, and the remainder of your party respectively) and a standard door in the north wall beyond which is a room with a locked door to equipment storage in its west wall:

Fortunately the detention terminal in the center of the first room allows you to unlock them all. Before doing so, make sure to remove any equipment from the character that you might want to equip on your next:

 

Captured by the Leviathan

|}

While Canderous and the rest of the crew head down to the docking hangar to board the Ebon Hawk, you, Bastila and Carth head to equipment storage. They equip themselves, and you can retrieve your own equipment and the party's inventory from the right of the two lockers by the south wall. There's also a backpack by the west wall in the southwest corner, a bandoleer by the north wall in the northwest corner, and a footlocker by the north wall:

Elevator
Juhani decloaks by the elevator at the east end of the prison block, ambushing and killing a Sith. The door to the elevator is behind her, but first she must travel down the corridor to the west. When she passes the T-junction, a Sith heavy trooper appears at the top of the ramp ahead:

Once the rest of the crew have been freed from their cells in  at the west end of the main corridor, and all your equipment and the party inventory have been retrieved from equipment storage, then you, Bastila and Carth must head up to the elevator at the east end of the prison block:

After opening the door to the elevator, use the elevator controls mounted in the east wall:
